Последние результаты

    Занятия за 4 недели

    Как пользоваться сайтом
    • Reading. Открой текст: слева текст и новые слова, справа вопросы. Включи таймер на 20 минут, ответь на вопросы и нажми «Проверить». Верные ответы подсветятся зелёным, ошибки красным с правильным вариантом.
    • Listening. Включи запись и отвечай по ходу. На экзамене запись звучит один раз, поэтому не останавливай её. Транскрипт открывай только после проверки.
    • Writing и Speaking. Сначала напиши или проговори ответ сам, потом открой образец и разбор. После задания нажми «Отметить как сделано».
    • Поиск сверху ищет по всем текстам, новым словам, вопросам и карточкам.
    • Прогресс сохраняется сам: ответы, баллы и отметки. Можно закрыть сайт и продолжить с того же места.
    • Тексты и записи составлены специально для этого набора в формате IELTS. Они короче экзаменационных: на экзамене текст Reading — 700–900 слов и 13–14 вопросов, секция Listening — 5–7 минут.

    Reading

    100 текстов, по 13 вопросов: True / False / Not Given, Yes / No / Not Given, multiple choice, completion, short answers, matching information и headings.

    Listening

    50 записей по 10 вопросов. Section 1 — бытовой диалог, Section 2 — монолог на бытовую тему, Section 3 — учебное обсуждение, Section 4 — лекция. Голоса британские и американские, мужские и женские.

    Полные тесты: 4 секции подряд

    Чтобы тренироваться как на экзамене, проходи 4 записи подряд без пауз (40 вопросов), потом сложи баллы. Когда все 4 секции теста пройдены, здесь появится итог и примерный балл.

    Перевод верных ответов в балл (из 40)

    Верных39–4037–3835–3632–3430–3126–2923–2518–2216–1713–15
    Балл98.587.576.565.554.5

    Таблица приблизительная: так обычно пересчитывают баллы Listening, но точная шкала немного меняется от теста к тесту. Секции здесь короче экзаменационных, поэтому балл — ориентир, а не прогноз.

    Про записи Cambridge

    Аудио из сборников Cambridge IELTS (в том числе 16) продаётся вместе с книгами и защищено авторским правом, поэтому его здесь нет. Записи выше озвучены синтезатором речи нейросетевыми британскими и американскими голосами в формате экзамена: вступление, 20 секунд на чтение вопросов, запись, полминуты на проверку. Настоящий экзаменационный звук бесплатно и легально есть в официальных пробных тестах British Council: takeielts.britishcouncil.org — free Listening practice tests. Сами книги Cambridge IELTS с аудио продаются в книжных магазинах и на сайте Cambridge.

    Настоящие подкасты для ежедневной практики

    Записи на этом сайте озвучены синтезатором. Чтобы привыкать к живой речи, слушай бесплатные подкасты на их сайтах — по одному выпуску в день.

    • BBC Learning English — 6 Minute English: 6 минут, два ведущих, есть транскрипт и словарь. Лучший старт для уровня 5.5–6.5.
    • BBC Learning English — The English We Speak: 3 минуты, разговорные выражения для Speaking.
    • BBC World Service — Global News Podcast: новости в естественном темпе, разные акценты.
    • BBC World Service — The History Hour и Discovery: история и наука — близко к Section 4.
    • BBC Radio 4 — Inside Science и In Our Time: академические обсуждения, уровень 7+.
    • TED Talks Daily: лекции 10–15 минут, американский акцент.
    • ABC — The Science Show: австралийский акцент, который тоже встречается на экзамене.

    Как слушать с пользой: первый раз без текста и запиши 5–10 ключевых фактов (цифры, имена, даты); второй раз с транскриптом; выпиши 5 новых выражений.

    Writing

    Содержание

    Вопросы ниже собраны из отчётов кандидатов за август–ноябрь 2026 и из сборников Cambridge IELTS 19–20. Формулировки пересказаны близко к экзаменационным. Официального списка «будущих вопросов» у IELTS нет: темы повторяются, поэтому это лучший материал для тренировки, но не гарантия.

    Формат и время

    ЗаданиеОбъёмВремяВесЧто оценивают
    Task 1 (Academic) — описание графика, таблицы, карты или процессаот 150 слов20 мин1/3Task Achievement, Coherence & Cohesion, Lexical Resource, Grammar
    Task 1 (General Training) — письмоот 150 слов20 мин1/3то же; важен тон (formal / informal)
    Task 2 — эссеот 250 слов40 мин2/3Task Response, Coherence & Cohesion, Lexical Resource, Grammar

    Task 1: метод Band 9 — четыре абзаца

    Ответы уровня Band 9 почти всегда устроены одинаково, какой бы ни была картинка: четыре абзаца, 150–190 слов. Длиннее писать не нужно: за лишние слова баллы не добавляют, а время на Task 2 теряется.

    АбзацЧто пишемПример начала
    1. IntroductionОдно предложение: перефразируй условие своими словами. Что показано, где, за какой период.The line graph compares… / The table gives information about…
    2. OverviewДва предложения о «большой картине» без цифр: общий тренд, самое большое и самое маленькое, главное различие. Это самый важный абзац: без него выше 5.0 за Task Achievement не поставят.It is clear that… / Overall, … / It is noticeable that…
    3. Details 1Цифры. Начни с первого года или с самой крупной группы. Сравнивай, а не перечисляй.In 1990, … compared with… / … while the figure for X was…
    4. Details 2Цифры для второй группы: последний год, пики, самые маленькие значения. Минимум 3 числа в абзаце.By 2020, … / By contrast, … / … respectively.

    Шесть правил, которые отличают Band 9

    1. Группируй, а не перечисляй. Никогда не описывай каждую линию, столбец или строку по очереди: экзаменатор ждёт сравнений.
    2. Не пытайся упомянуть всё. Выбери ключевое: первый и последний год, пики, самое большое и самое маленькое, самые сильные изменения. Средние значения можно пропустить.
    3. В overview нет цифр. Только слова вроде overall increase, the highest, the lowest, the most significant change.
    4. Время глагола зависит от дат. Прошлые годы — past simple (rose, fell), будущее — will / is expected to / is predicted to, без дат (таблицы, процессы, схемы) — present simple.
    5. Только то, что на картинке. Никаких причин, мнений и выводов от себя.
    6. Цифры точные. Ошибка в числе снижает Task Achievement, даже если английский отличный. Приблизительность передавай словами: just over, almost, roughly.

    Язык Task 1: что использовать

    • Overview: It is clear that… · Overall, … · It is noticeable that… · The most significant change was… · X accounted for the largest proportion of…
    • Рост: rise, increase, grow, climb; сильный — surge, soar, jump; a sharp / steady / gradual / slight increase
    • Падение: fall, decline, decrease, drop, dip; plummet, plunge; a dramatic / slight fall
    • Стабильность и пики: remain stable, level off, fluctuate; peak at, reach a peak of, hit a low of
    • Значение: stood at, was, reached, accounted for, made up, constituted · the figure for X · the proportion of
    • Сравнение: compared with, while, whereas, by contrast, twice as high as, three times the figure for, considerably higher than
    • Приблизительность: just over, just under, almost, nearly, roughly, approximately, around a quarter, more than half
    • Экономия слов: … at 6% and 4% respectively · the figures for X and Y were…

    Четыре грамматических приёма, которые поднимают оценку

    1. -ing оборот после запятой добавляет деталь к тренду: Sales rose steadily, reaching a peak of 250,000 in 2018.
    2. with + существительное (+ -ing): Sport came second, with 6 hours a week. · Prices rose in all cities, with London seeing the largest increase.
    3. Глагол ↔ существительное, чтобы не повторяться: Sales dropped sharply → There was a sharp drop in sales.
    4. Прогнозы: The figure is expected to reach 35%. · It is predicted that the number will rise.

    В конце раздела — упражнения на эти приёмы с автоматической проверкой.

    Task 1 Academic — что реально попадалось (август–ноябрь 2026)

    1. Line graph — уровень занятости мужчин и женщин 18–34 лет в Австралии, 1976–2011 (25 сен и 28 окт 2026)
    2. Table — число автомобилей на 1 000 жителей в восьми странах, 1990 и 2000 (25 окт 2026)
    3. Map — план этажа музея в 1998 и 2008 (18 окт 2026)
    4. Maps — жилой квартал сейчас и план будущей застройки (14 окт 2026)
    5. Table — использование интернета взрослыми в одной европейской стране, 2006–2010 (12 авг 2026)
    6. Process — производство керамических горшков (1 авг 2026)
    7. Bar chart — продажи автопроизводителя по регионам, 2006–2010, % (июль 2026)
    8. Bar chart — средний возраст выхода на пенсию мужчин и женщин в семи странах, 2004 и 2008 (июль 2026)
    9. Chart — расходы домохозяйств на товары и услуги, 1995–2005 (июль 2026)
    10. Chart + table — средний заработок по отраслям (июль 2026)
    11. Table — временные трудовые мигранты в четырёх странах, 2003 и 2006 (март 2026)
    12. Graphs — количество выпущенных фильмов и продажи билетов, 1996 и 2000 (апрель 2026)

    Ниже 23 тренировочных задания по всем типам картинок, в том числе на эти темы. Цифры в них учебные (придуманы для практики), а не с экзамена. К каждому заданию есть образец уровня Band 9 в четыре абзаца с планом, лексикой и разбором: сначала напиши свой ответ за 20 минут, потом открой образец.

    Line graph — линейный график

    Что показывает: изменения во времени. Как писать:

    • В overview опиши, что произошло со всеми линиями от первого года до последнего: есть ли общий тренд, какая линия выше всех, где самое резкое изменение.
    • Если лет много, все не упоминай. Ключевые точки: первый год, последний год и «особые» годы (пик, резкий рост или падение).
    • Первый абзац деталей начни со сравнения линий в первом году: In 1990, the figure for X was…, compared with…
    • Второй абзац — что произошло дальше и чем всё закончилось.
    • Прошлые годы — past simple; прогноз на будущее — is expected / predicted / projected to.

    Practice 1 — Line graph

    The graph below shows the employment rates of men and women aged 18–34 in Australia between 1976 and 2011. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
    Employment rate (%)19761981198619911996200120062011
    Men8986847879808381
    Women5256616366697273
    Образец (Band 9), 178 слов

    The line graph compares the proportions of Australian men and women aged 18 to 34 who were in work over a 35-year period from 1976 to 2011.

    Overall, although men were more likely to be employed throughout the period, the gap between the sexes narrowed considerably, as the female rate rose steadily while the male rate fell slightly.

    In 1976, almost nine in ten young men (89%) had a job, compared with just over half of young women (52%). Male employment then declined gradually to 84% in 1986 before dropping more sharply to a low of 78% in 1991. After that it recovered slowly, reaching 83% in 2006, and ended the period at 81%, eight percentage points below its starting level.

    By contrast, the figure for women increased in every five-year period. It climbed from 52% to 63% by 1991 and continued to rise to 72% in 2006, before levelling off at 73% in 2011. As a result, the difference between the two groups shrank from 37 percentage points at the beginning to only 8 by the end.

    Practice 2 — Line graph with a forecast

    The graph below shows the percentage of the population aged 65 and over in four countries between 1960 and 2020, with projections for 2040. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
    Population aged 65+ (%)19601980200020202040*
    Japan69172935
    Germany1116162230
    USA911121722
    Nigeria33334

    * 2040 — прогноз. Обрати внимание на времена: прошлое в past simple, прогноз через is expected / predicted to.

    Образец (Band 9), 187 слов — план, лексика, разбор
    План: Line graph с прогнозом. Overview: рост в трёх странах из четырёх; самое резкое изменение — Япония, Нигерия почти без изменений. Детали 1: 1960 и путь до 2000 (Япония обгоняет). Детали 2: 2020 и прогноз на 2040.

    The line graph compares the proportion of people aged 65 or over in Japan, Germany, the USA and Nigeria between 1960 and 2020, and gives predictions up to 2040.

    It is clear that the elderly population grew in three of the four countries and is expected to continue rising. Japan saw the most dramatic change, while the figure for Nigeria remained almost unchanged throughout the period.

    In 1960, Germany had the highest proportion of older people, at 11%, compared with 9% in the USA and only 6% in Japan. Just 3% of Nigerians were aged 65 or over. Over the next forty years, the figure for Japan rose steeply to 17%, overtaking both Germany (16%) and the USA (12%).

    By 2020, almost three in ten Japanese people (29%) were 65 or older, while the figures for Germany and the USA stood at 22% and 17% respectively. By 2040, the proportion in Japan is predicted to reach 35%, and Germany is expected to follow closely at 30%. The figure for the USA is projected to rise to 22%, whereas in Nigeria it will remain at only around 4%.

    Полезная лексика из образца (выделена в тексте)
    the proportion of people aged 65 or overдоля людей в возрасте 65 лет и старше
    gives predictions up to 2040даёт прогноз до 2040 года
    the elderly populationпожилое население
    is expected to continue risingожидается, что продолжит расти
    remained almost unchangedпочти не изменилась
    rose steeplyрезко выросла
    overtakingобогнав-ing оборот
    almost three in tenпочти трое из десятиспособ сказать 29% словами
    stood atсоставляли
    is predicted to reachпо прогнозу достигнет
    is expected to follow closelyожидается, что будет следовать вплотную
    is projected to riseпрогнозируется рост
    Разбор: Детали начинаются со сравнения всех линий в первом году — как советует метод. Прошлое в past simple, будущее через is predicted / is expected / is projected to, без повторов. Respectively экономит слова. Особая точка — момент, когда Япония обгоняет остальных.

    Bar chart — столбчатая диаграмма

    Что показывает: сравнение категорий, иногда в разные годы. Как писать:

    • Сначала пойми, что сравнивается: категории между собой, годы или и то и другое.
    • Overview: самая большая и самая маленькая категории и главное изменение между годами.
    • Детали удобно делить по годам (первый год / последний год) или по группам (выросли / упали).
    • Если на диаграмме нет лет, пиши в present simple.
    • Stacked bar (полосы по 100%): сравнивай доли внутри каждой полосы и называй «лидера» в каждой стране. Population pyramid — это тоже столбчатая диаграмма: складывай мужчин и женщин в возрастной группе и сравнивай форму (широкое основание = много детей, широкий верх = старое население).

    Practice 3 — Bar chart

    The chart below shows the average retirement age of men and women in seven countries in 2008. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
    Average retirement ageKoreaJapanUSASwedenAustraliaItalyFrance
    Men71696566646159
    Women68666463626060
    Образец (Band 9), 190 слов — план, лексика, разбор
    План: Столбчатая диаграмма, 7 стран, мужчины и женщины. Overview: мужчины уходят позже почти везде; самая поздняя пенсия в Корее, самая ранняя во Франции/Италии.

    The bar chart compares the average age at which men and women retired in seven countries in 2008.

    Overall, men tended to retire later than women in almost every country. People in Korea and Japan stopped working at the oldest ages, whereas the earliest retirement was found in France and Italy.

    Korea stood out with the highest figures for both sexes: men retired at an average age of 71 and women at 68. Japan came second, with ages of 69 and 66 respectively. In both of these countries, women left work three years earlier than men, which was the largest gender gap shown.

    The United States, Sweden and Australia formed a middle group, with men retiring at between 64 and 66 and women at between 62 and 64. The difference between the sexes here was smaller, only one year in the USA and two or three years in the other two countries. At the other end of the scale, Italian men retired at 61 and women at 60, while France was the only country where women did not retire earlier than men, both doing so at around 59 to 60.

    left workуходили с работы

    The difference between the sexesразница между полами
    At the other end of the scaleна другом конце шкалыпереход к самым низким значениям
    was the only country whereединственная страна, гдевыделяет исключение
    Разбор: Исключение (Франция) отмечено отдельно — экзаменатор ищет именно такие детали. Respectively экономит слова. Не пытайся перечислить все 14 чисел — группируй.

    Practice 4 — Bar chart

    The chart below shows the percentage of a car manufacturer's total sales in four regions from 2006 to 2010. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
    Share of total sales (%)20062007200820092010
    North America4240353128
    Europe3030292726
    Asia1820253034
    South America1010111212
    Образец (Band 9), 182 слов — план, лексика, разбор
    План: Столбчатая диаграмма, доли продаж по 4 регионам за 5 лет. Overview: Северная Америка упала, Азия выросла и стала лидером; Европа слегка снизилась, Южная Америка мала и стабильна.

    The bar chart illustrates how the share of a car manufacturer's total sales was divided among four regions between 2006 and 2010.

    Overall, the company's sales shifted from North America towards Asia. While North America accounted for the largest share at the beginning of the period, Asia had overtaken it by the end. Europe's share declined slightly, and South America remained the smallest market throughout.

    In 2006, North America represented 42% of sales, but this proportion fell every year, dropping to just 28% in 2010. Asia showed the opposite trend. Its share almost doubled, rising from 18% to 34%, and it surpassed North America in 2009, when it reached 30% compared with 31% for North America, before clearly taking the lead in the final year.

    Europe's contribution was relatively stable, remaining at 30% in the first two years and then edging down to 26%. South America consistently accounted for the smallest proportion of sales, although its share increased slightly from 10% to 12%. By 2010, therefore, Asia, North America and Europe each contributed roughly a quarter to a third of total sales.

    Полезная лексика из образца (выделена в тексте)

    shifted from North America towards Asiaсместились от … к …описывает перераспределение долей
    accounted for the largest shareсоставляла наибольшую долю

    showed the opposite trendпоказала противоположную тенденцию
    surpassedпревзошла
    taking the leadвыходя вперёд
    relatively stableотносительно стабильной
    edging downпонемногу снижаясь
    consistently accounted for the smallest proportionнеизменно составляла наименьшую долю

    Разбор: Внимание: в 2009 Азия (30%) ещё чуть ниже Северной Америки (31%) — в тексте это учтено. Проверяй каждую цифру, неточности снижают Task Achievement. Opposite trend — хорошая связка между абзацами.

    Practice 5 — Bar chart, two years

    The chart below shows the average number of hours per week that teenagers in one country spent on five leisure activities in 2005 and 2025. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
    Hours per weekTVSocial mediaVideo gamesSportReading
    2005142564
    2025515942
    Образец (Band 9), 172 слов — план, лексика, разбор
    План: Bar chart, два года, пять категорий. Overview: сдвиг от ТВ к соцсетям; соцсети с последнего места на первое; спорт и чтение упали. Детали 1: 2005. Детали 2: 2025 и изменения.

    The bar chart compares the average number of hours that teenagers spent each week on five leisure activities in 2005 and 2025.

    Overall, there was a clear shift from watching television towards screen-based activities on phones and computers. Social media went from being the least popular activity to the most popular, while the time spent on sport and reading fell.

    In 2005, television dominated teenagers' free time, at 14 hours per week, which was more than the other four activities combined. Sport came second, with 6 hours, followed by video games (5 hours) and reading (4 hours). Young people spent only 2 hours a week on social media.

    Twenty years later, the situation had almost reversed. Time spent on social media rose more than sevenfold to 15 hours, and the figure for video games almost doubled to 9 hours. By contrast, television viewing dropped sharply to just 5 hours a week. Sport and reading also declined, to 4 hours and 2 hours respectively, making reading the least popular of the five activities.

    Полезная лексика из образца (выделена в тексте)

    The chart compares the proportions of secondary school students in five countries who travel to school on foot, by bicycle, by bus or by car.

    Overall, the most common way of getting to school varies considerably between the countries. Students in the Netherlands and Japan rarely travel by car, whereas in the USA and Australia the car is the most popular option.

    Cycling is far more common in the Netherlands than anywhere else, accounting for more than half of all journeys to school (55%).     The charts compare the age structure of the populations of Nigeria and Japan in 2025, broken down by gender.

    It is clear that the two countries have very different population profiles. Nigeria has a typical pyramid shape, with a large proportion of children and young adults, whereas Japan's population is dominated by middle-aged and older people.

    In Nigeria, children aged 0 to 14 make up 41.4% of the population, and a further 27.4% are aged 15 to 29. The size of each age group then falls steadily, so that people aged 60 or over account for only 4.3% of the total. There is very little difference between the figures for males and females in any age group.

    Japan, by contrast, has a much smaller proportion of children, at just 11.5%. The largest groups are those aged 45 to 59 (20.3%) and 75 or over (20.5%). Women outnumber men significantly in the oldest group, at 12.6% compared with 7.9%, which is the largest gender gap shown on either chart.

    Table — таблица

    Что показывает: много чисел сразу. Главное — не утонуть в них. Как писать:

    • Перед письмом отметь ключевые числа: самое большое в каждом столбце и строке, самые сильные изменения. Средние значения можно игнорировать.
    • В overview сравнивай целые категории (столбцы или строки), а не отдельные клетки. Если не получается — сравни самое большое и самое маленькое. Два предложения.
    • Раздели отмеченные числа на две группы, по одной на абзац: например, все самые высокие значения вместе, все самые низкие вместе. Не описывай столбцы по очереди.
    • В каждом абзаце деталей — минимум 3 числа.
    • Нет дат — present simple.

    The table below shows the number of motor vehicles per 1,000 inhabitants in eight countries in 1990 and 2000. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
    Vehicles per 1,000 peopleUSAItalyGermanyJapanPolandBrazilChinaIndia
    19907525294854681688754
    2000779656572570312118128

    Подсказка: сгруппируй страны — высокий уровень (США, Италия, Германия, Япония), средний (Польша, Бразилия), низкий (Китай, Индия). Отметь, что рост был везде, а самый быстрый относительный рост — в Польше и Китае.

    Образец (Band 9), 189 слов — план, лексика, разбор
    План: Таблица, два года, 8 стран. Группировка: высокий уровень (4 богатые страны), средний (Польша, Бразилия), очень низкий (Китай, Индия). Overview: рост везде; разрыв между группами огромный.

    The table compares the number of motor vehicles for every thousand people in eight countries in 1990 and 2000.

    Overall, car ownership increased in all eight countries over the decade, but there was a vast gap between the wealthy nations, where vehicles were extremely common, and China and India, where they remained rare.

    The United States had by far the highest rate in both years, rising slightly from 752 to 779 vehicles per thousand inhabitants. Italy, Germany and Japan followed, with figures of between roughly 470 and 530 in 1990. Of these three, Italy saw the largest increase, reaching 656, while Germany and Japan both ended the period at just over 570.

    Poland and Brazil occupied a middle position. Poland recorded the most dramatic relative growth of any country, with its figure almost doubling from 168 to 312, whereas the number in Brazil grew more modestly, from 87 to 118. At the bottom of the table, China and India had only five and four vehicles per thousand people respectively in 1990. Although both figures roughly doubled, to 12 and 8, they were still tiny compared with the other nations.

    Practice 9 — Table

    The table below gives information about the percentage of adults in one European country who used the internet between 2006 and 2010, by age group. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

    The table shows the percentage of adults in four age groups who used the internet in a European country each year from 2006 to 2010.

    Overall, internet use rose steadily in every age group. Younger people were consistently the most likely to be online, but the gap between the generations narrowed, as the fastest growth occurred among older adults.

    In 2006, the overwhelming majority of 16 to 24-year-olds (88%) were already internet users, and this figure climbed gradually to an almost universal 98% by 2010. The 25 to 44 age group followed a similar pattern at a slightly lower level, increasing from 76% to 92% over the five years.

    Among those aged 45 to 64, just over half (55%) used the internet at the start of the period, but the proportion grew by around six percentage points a year to reach 79%. The most striking change, however, was seen in the oldest group. Only 15% of people aged 65 and over were online in 2006, yet this proportion more than doubled to 38% in 2010. Even so, it remained far below the figures for all younger groups.

    It is clear that Toronto has by far the largest library system, while residents of Helsinki are the most frequent library users. Sydney has the smallest network on almost every measure.

    Toronto has 100 libraries holding 10.4 million books, a collection more than three times the size of any other shown.     Pie chart — круговые диаграммы

    Что показывает: доли целого, обычно для двух лет или нескольких групп. Как писать:

    • Overview: самая большая доля и главное изменение или различие между диаграммами.
    • Язык долей: accounted for, made up, constituted, the largest proportion, a quarter, just over a third, more than half.

    The pie charts compare how energy was used in homes in one country in 1990 and 2020.

    Overall, heating accounted for the largest share of household energy in both years, although its dominance declined. The most significant growth was in the proportion of energy used to run household appliances.

    In 1990, more than half of all domestic energy (58%) went on heating. Hot water was the second largest category, at 18%, while appliances, lighting and cooking together made up less than a quarter of the total, at 10%, 8% and 6% respectively.

    By 2020, the share used for heating had fallen to 42%. Meanwhile, the figure for appliances more than doubled to 22%, overtaking hot water (20%) to become the second largest category.     • Overview: главные изменения в целом (стало больше жилья, появились дороги, исчезли деревья) или главное различие между двумя местами.
    • Детали — по периодам или по частям карты (север / юг, вход / залы). Для двух мест — абзац на каждое.
    • Прошлое — past simple и пассив: was demolished, was replaced by, was converted into. План на будущее — will be built, is going to be extended.
    • Указывай расположение: to the north of, next to, opposite, in the south-west corner, alongside the railway.

    Process и diagram — процессы и схемы

    Что показывает: как что-то делается или происходит в природе, либо сравнение двух устройств. Как писать:

    • Вступление — перефраз задания.
    • Overview: сколько этапов в процессе, с чего он начинается и чем заканчивается.
    • Опиши каждый этап. Удобно разбить описание на два абзаца, начав второй где-то в середине процесса.
    • Слова последовательности: at the first / following / final stage, next, after that, once…, finally.
    • Present simple. Для производственных процессов — пассив: the bricks are heated. Для природных циклов часто естественнее актив: the fish swim back to the river.
    • Если на схеме не процесс, а сравнение двух устройств, пиши как о таблице: overview — главное различие, детали — по одному абзацу на каждое устройство.

    Practice 19 — Process

    The diagram below shows the process by which ceramic pots are manufactured. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
    1. Raw clay is dug out of the ground by an excavator and transported by lorry to the factory.
    2. The clay is crushed and passed through a sieve to remove stones.
    3. Water is added in a mixing tank; the liquid clay is poured into moulds.
    4. The moulds are left for 4–6 hours; the pots are then removed and smoothed by hand.
    5. Pots are placed in a drying room (2 days, 40°C).
    6. First firing in a kiln at 1,000°C.
    7. Pots are painted and coated with glaze.
    8. Second firing at 1,200°C; cooling for 24 hours.
    9. Quality check → packaging → delivery to shops.

    Подсказка: в overview укажи число этапов и где процесс начинается и заканчивается (Overall, there are nine main stages, beginning with the extraction of clay and ending with the delivery of finished pots). Используй пассив и связки последовательности.

    Образец (Band 9), 192 слов — план, лексика, разбор
    План: Процесс, 9 стадий. Overview: число стадий, начало (добыча глины) и конец (доставка). Body 1 — подготовка и формовка. Body 2 — сушка, обжиг, роспись, контроль. Пассив везде.

    The diagram shows the stages involved in the manufacture of ceramic pots.

    Overall, there are nine main stages in the process, beginning with the extraction of raw clay from the ground and ending with the delivery of the finished pots to shops. The pots are fired in a kiln twice.

    First, clay is dug out of the ground by an excavator and taken by lorry to the factory. There it is crushed and passed through a sieve in order to remove any stones. Water is then added in a mixing tank, and the resulting liquid clay is poured into moulds. After four to six hours, the pots are removed from the moulds and smoothed by hand.

    Next, the pots are placed in a drying room, where they are left for two days at a temperature of 40°C. They then undergo their first firing in a kiln at 1,000°C. After this, they are painted and coated with glaze before being fired a second time at an even higher temperature of 1,200°C. Once they have cooled for 24 hours, each pot is checked for quality. Finally, the pots are packaged and delivered to shops.

    Practice 20 — Process: a natural cycle

    The diagram below shows the life cycle of the salmon. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features. Write at least 150 words.
    1. Eggs — laid among small stones (gravel) in shallow water in the upper river.
    2. Alevin — tiny fish hatch after about 3 months; stay hidden in the gravel for about 6 weeks, feeding on a yolk sac.
    3. Fry — swim freely in the river and feed on insects for up to 1 year.
    4. Smolt — 12–15 cm long; travel downstream to the sea.
    5. Adult salmon — live in the ocean for 1–4 years; grow to 70–80 cm.
    6. Return — swim back up the river where they hatched and lay eggs → the cycle starts again.
    Образец (Band 9), 195 слов — план, лексика, разбор
    План: Process (природный цикл). Overview: шесть этапов, часть в реке, часть в море; начинается и заканчивается в верховье реки. Детали 1: этапы 1–3 в реке. Детали 2: этапы 4–6 и возвращение.

    The diagram illustrates the life cycle of the salmon, from eggs in a river to adult fish in the ocean.

    There are six main stages in the cycle, which takes place partly in fresh water and partly in the sea. It begins and ends in the upper part of a river, where eggs are laid.

    At the first stage, salmon eggs are laid among small stones in shallow river water. After around three months, they hatch into tiny fish called alevin, which remain hidden in the gravel for about six weeks, feeding on a yolk sac attached to their bodies. Once this food source is used up, the young fish, now known as fry, swim freely in the river and feed on insects for up to a year.

    In the next stage, the fish, which have grown to between 12 and 15 centimetres and are called smolt, travel downstream to the sea. They spend the following one to four years in the ocean, where they become adults measuring 70 to 80 centimetres. Finally, the adult salmon swim back to the river in which they hatched, where they lay their eggs and the cycle begins again.

Для природного цикла уместен актив (swim, travel), пассив только там, где действие не выполняет сама рыба (eggs are laid). Последовательность: At the first stage, After, Once, In the next stage, Finally.

    Practice 21 — Process: manufacturing / recycling

    The diagram below shows the process by which used glass bottles are recycled. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features. Write at least 150 words.
    1. Collection — used bottles are left in bottle banks and collected
    2. Transport — by lorry to a recycling plant
    3. Cleaning — washed with high-pressure water
    4. Sorting — by colour: green, brown, clear
    5. Crushing — into small pieces (“cullet”)
    6. Melting — cullet + sand, soda ash, limestone; furnace at 1,500°C
    7. Moulding — liquid glass poured into moulds; new bottles cool
    8. Filling & delivery — filled with drinks, sent to shops, bought by consumers

    Подсказка Simon: в overview — число этапов, начало и конец, и то, что процесс цикличный. Пассив почти везде: are collected, is crushed, is poured. Раздели этапы на два абзаца (например, 1–5 и 6–8).

    Образец (Band 9), 169 слов — план, лексика, разбор
    План: Процесс, сделанный человеком → пассив и present simple. Абзац 1 — перефраз. Абзац 2 — overview: восемь этапов, начало и конец, процесс цикличный. Абзац 3 — этапы 1–5 (сбор → дробление). Абзац 4 — этапы 6–8 (плавка → магазины) и возврат к началу.

    The diagram illustrates the process by which used glass bottles are recycled.

    Overall, there are eight stages in the process, beginning with the collection of empty bottles and ending with the sale of new ones. The process is cyclical, because the new bottles can eventually be recycled again.

    At the first stage, used glass bottles are left in bottle banks, from which they are collected and transported by lorry to a recycling plant. There, the bottles are cleaned with high-pressure water before being sorted by colour into three groups: green, brown and clear glass. Each type of glass is then crushed into small pieces, known as cullet.

    In the next step, the cullet is mixed with sand, soda ash and limestone and melted in a furnace at a temperature of 1,500°C. The liquid glass is poured into moulds to form new bottles, which are left to cool. Finally, the bottles are filled with drinks and delivered to shops, where they are bought by consumers, and the cycle begins again.

    Practice 22 — Diagram: how a system works

    The diagram below shows how a pumped-storage hydroelectric power station operates during the day and at night. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features. Write at least 150 words.

    Day — electricity is produced

    1. Water held behind a dam in a high-level reservoir
    2. Intake gates open; water flows down a large pipe
    3. Water drives reversible turbines in the power station
    4. Turbines turn generators → electricity
    5. Power lines carry electricity to the national grid; water flows into a low-level reservoir

    Night — water is pumped back

    1. Demand for electricity is low; cheap power from the grid
    2. Turbines run in reverse and work as pumps
    3. Water pumped from the low-level reservoir back up to the high-level reservoir
    4. Ready for use the next day

    Это не «процесс производства», а схема работы устройства. Структура та же: overview — две фазы (день и ночь), затем по абзацу на каждую.

    Образец (Band 9), 186 слов — план, лексика, разбор
    План: Схема работы устройства. Абзац 1 — перефраз. Абзац 2 — overview: две фазы (день — вода вниз и электричество; ночь — вода наверх). Абзац 3 — дневная фаза по шагам. Абзац 4 — ночная фаза. Present simple, пассив там, где действует машина.

    The diagram shows how a pumped-storage hydroelectric power station generates electricity, and how it operates differently during the day and at night.

    Overall, the system works in two phases. During the day, water flows downhill from a high reservoir to a low one, producing electricity, while at night the same water is pumped back up so that the cycle can be repeated.

    In the daytime, water is held behind a dam in the high-level reservoir. When electricity is needed, the gates of an intake are opened, and the water rushes down a large pipe to the power station. There, it drives reversible turbines, which turn generators to produce electricity. This electricity is then carried by power lines to the national grid, while the water flows into a low-level reservoir.

    At night, when demand for electricity is lower, the process is reversed. Cheap electricity from the grid is used to run the turbines in the opposite direction, so that they work as pumps. As a result, water is pumped from the low-level reservoir back up to the high-level reservoir, ready to be used again the following day.

    Разбор: Это не производство, а устройство, поэтому overview описывает не «этапы», а две фазы работы. Каждый абзац деталей = одна фаза, и в каждом есть связка времени (In the daytime / At night). Пассив чередуется с активом: вода «течёт» сама (flows, rushes), а люди и машины делают что-то с ней (is held, is pumped). Причинно-следственные связки (so that, As a result) показывают, как части системы связаны, — это поднимает Coherence.

    Practice 23 — Diagram: comparing two systems

    The diagrams below show two methods of irrigating crops. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.

    Описание схем (на экзамене это будут рисунки):

    Flood irrigationDrip irrigation
    Источник водыriver or canal → open channelstank → pump → filter → plastic pipes
    Как вода доходит до растенийthe whole field is covered with waterwater drips from small holes next to each plant
    Вода за сезон, на гектарabout 12,000 m³about 5,000 m³
    Потери (испарение, стекание)about 50%less than 10%
    Стоимость оборудованияlowhigh

    Образец (Band 9), 180 слов — план, лексика, разбор
    План: Diagram-сравнение двух систем (не процесс). Overview: главное различие — как вода доходит до растений; капельный расходует меньше, но дороже. Детали 1: затопление. Детали 2: капельный.

    The diagrams compare two methods of irrigating crops: flood irrigation and drip irrigation.

    The most noticeable difference between the two systems is the way in which water reaches the plants. Drip irrigation uses far less water than flooding, but it requires more expensive equipment.

    In flood irrigation, water flows from a river or canal along open channels and is allowed to cover the whole field. This method uses around 12,000 cubic metres of water per hectare in a growing season, and about half of this is lost through evaporation and runoff. However, the equipment needed is simple and cheap, and the system is well suited to flat land and crops such as rice.

    Drip irrigation, by contrast, delivers water from a tank through a network of plastic pipes, using a pump and a filter. The water drips slowly from small holes next to each plant, so less than 10% is wasted, and only 5,000 cubic metres are needed per hectare. Although the system is costly to install, it can be used on slopes and is ideal for fruit and vegetables.

    Task 2: метод Band 9 (Simon)

    Все образцы Task 2 ниже написаны по методу из сборника Simon «Band 9 Essays»: четыре абзаца, 250–300 слов, простой и ясный язык. Simon — бывший экзаменатор IELTS, и главный его совет звучит так: не пытайся впечатлить сложной грамматикой, а ответь на вопрос и объясни свои идеи последовательно.

    Что происходит «в голове» перед письмом: 10 шагов

    1. Прочитай вопрос внимательно, 2–3 раза. Спроси себя: какая тема и о чём именно меня просят написать?
    2. Подчеркни всё, что обязательно должно быть в эссе. Отвечай на каждую часть вопроса.
    3. Реши, что пойдёт в каждый из четырёх абзацев. Любой тип эссе укладывается в четыре абзаца.
    4. Если нужно мнение, выбери то, которое легче всего объяснить и для которого ты знаешь хорошую лексику, а не то, что «правильнее».
    5. Набросай слова и выражения по теме.
    6. Вступление — два предложения: тема своими словами + простой ответ (с мнением, если его просят).
    7. Каждый основной абзац начни с короткого тематического предложения, потом развивай мысль: объяснение → пример.
    8. Время от времени перечитывай вопрос: отвечаешь ли ты на все его части?
    9. Считай слова по строкам: примерно 10 слов в строке — так быстро видно, сколько написано.
    10. Не хватает до 250 — расширь один из примеров в основном абзаце, а не вывод.

    Шесть правил

    • «I» можно. Если вопрос спрашивает твоё мнение (Do you agree?), пиши I believe, in my opinion. Совет «не писать I» относится к университетским работам, не к IELTS.
    • Полностью согласен / не согласен — позиция во вступлении и выводе; в абзаце 2 одна причина, в абзаце 3 другая. Не пиши абзац о том, что думают другие, иначе получится «discuss both views». Противоположный довод можно упомянуть, только чтобы опровергнуть его.
    • Частично согласен — во вступлении и выводе ясно, что ты принимаешь обе стороны в какой-то степени. По абзацу на каждую сторону, но от себя: On the one hand, I accept that… / On the other hand, I also believe that…
    • Discuss both views + opinion — своё мнение уже во вступлении, а не только в выводе. Свою сторону ставь вторым абзацем.
    • Уверенность быть «простым». Не надо втискивать пассив, условные предложения и «академические» слова. Простое не значит лёгкое: нужна точность и ясность.
    • Вывод — одно предложение, которое повторяет ответ. Никаких новых идей.

    Формула основного абзаца

    Тематическое предложение (о чём абзац) → объяснение (почему) → пример (For example, …; можно личный или придуманный правдоподобный) → результат (As a result, … / In other words, …). Примеры можно придумывать: Simon сам пишет, что это нормально.

    Task 2: шаблоны Simon по типам вопросов

    Это каркасы из образцов Simon. Слова в скобках меняются под тему. Каждый образец ниже помечен, по какому шаблону он написан.

    ТипВступление (2 предложения)Абзац 2Абзац 3Вывод
    Opinion: полностью за / против
    To what extent do you agree or disagree?    		Some people believe that [тема]. I completely agree / disagree with this view.In my opinion, [довод 1]. For example, …I also believe that [довод 2]. / The argument in favour of [X] would be that… However, I believe this to be a very short-sighted view.In conclusion, I (do not) believe that…
    Opinion: частичноIt is true that [тема]. While I agree that [A], I believe that [B].On the one hand, I accept that…On the other hand, I (also) believe that…In conclusion, although [A], …[B].
    Discussion
    Discuss both views and give your opinion    		People have different views about [тема]. While some argue that [A], I believe that [B].On the one hand, there are several reasons why some people believe that [A]. Firstly, … Secondly, …On the other hand, I would argue that [B]. / I agree with those who argue that…In conclusion, while there are good reasons why…, in my opinion…
    Advantages / disadvantages
    Do the advantages outweigh…?    		It is true that [тема]. While I accept that [it has some benefits], I believe that [the drawbacks are more significant].On the one hand, [X] can be…However, I would argue that these benefits are outweighed by the drawbacks.In conclusion, it seems to me that…
    Positive / negative developmentIt is true that [тема]. Although there are some drawbacks…, I would argue that there are far more benefits.The main drawback of [X] is that…Despite the negatives mentioned above, I believe that [X] is a positive development for various reasons. Firstly, … Secondly, … Finally, …In conclusion, while I recognise the possible disadvantages of [X], I consider it to be a positive development overall.
    Causes / problems + solutionsIt is true that [тема]. There are several reasons for this, but [governments / individuals] could take steps to [решить].There are various reasons why… Firstly, … Secondly, … Finally, …However, there are several steps that could be taken to… A simple solution would be to… A second measure would be…In conclusion, various measures can be taken to tackle…
    Two-part question
    Why…? Is it positive or negative?    		It is true that [тема]. There could be several reasons for this, and I consider it to be a [positive / negative] trend.Ответ на вопрос 1Ответ на вопрос 2: In my view, the changes described above should be seen as…In conclusion, [ответ 1], and I believe that [ответ 2].

    Если в вопросе три части (например: какие проблемы? что может сделать государство? что могут сделать люди?), Simon пишет пять абзацев: вступление, по абзацу на каждую часть, вывод.

    Связки, которые Simon использует постоянно

    • Порядок: Firstly, … Secondly, … Finally, … · Another reason is that… · A further point is that…
    • Мнение: In my opinion · I believe that · I would argue that · It seems to me that · Personally, …
    • Уступка и поворот: It is true that…, but… · While I accept that… · On the one hand / On the other hand · However, … · Despite this, …
    • Пример и пояснение: For example, … · To take [the UK] as an example, … · In other words, … · In my experience, …
    • Следствие: As a result, … · This means that… · Therefore, … · This can only lead to…

    Частые ошибки, которые стоят баллов

    • Ответ не на все части вопроса — потолок 5.0–6.0 за Task Response.
    • Позиция неясная или меняется от вступления к выводу.
    • Абзац «Some people think… other people think…» в эссе agree/disagree.
    • Список из пяти коротких доводов без объяснений: лучше два довода с объяснением и примером.
    • Меньше 250 слов. Больше 300 не нужно: баллы за длину не добавляют, а риск ошибок растёт.

    Упражнение 7. Определи тип вопроса Task 2

    От типа вопроса зависит шаблон эссе. Выбери тип для каждого вопроса.

    Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

    1 Some people think that zoos should be closed. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
    • A Opinion (agree / disagree)
    • B Discuss both views + opinion
    • C Advantages / disadvantages (positive / negative)
    • D Causes / problems + solutions
     ✔ A
    2 Some people believe that children should start school at the age of four, while others think they should start at seven. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
    • A Opinion (agree / disagree)
    • B Discuss both views + opinion
    • C Advantages / disadvantages (positive / negative)
    • D Causes / problems + solutions
     ✔ B
    3 More and more people work from home. Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages?
    • A Opinion (agree / disagree)
    • B Discuss both views + opinion
    • C Advantages / disadvantages (positive / negative)
    • D Causes / problems + solutions
     ✔ C
    4 Many cities suffer from traffic congestion. What are the causes? What measures could be taken to reduce it?
    • A Opinion (agree / disagree)
    • B Discuss both views + opinion
    • C Advantages / disadvantages (positive / negative)
    • D Causes / problems + solutions
     ✔ D
    5 Nowadays many people choose to do their shopping online. Is this a positive or negative development?
    • A Opinion (agree / disagree)
    • B Discuss both views + opinion
    • C Advantages / disadvantages (positive / negative)
    • D Causes / problems + solutions
     ✔ C
    6 Obesity among children is increasing in many countries. Why is this happening? How can the problem be solved?
    • A Opinion (agree / disagree)
    • B Discuss both views + opinion
    • C Advantages / disadvantages (positive / negative)

    Упражнение 8. Вступление и вывод по Simon

    Выбери лучший вариант. Помни правило Simon: вступление — 2 предложения (тема своими словами + твой ответ), вывод — 1 предложение.

    Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

    1 Question: Zoos should be closed. Agree or disagree? Which introduction is best?
    • A Zoos are a very interesting topic, and people have many different opinions about them, which I will discuss in this essay.
    • B It is true that some people want zoos to be closed. I completely disagree with this view, because I believe that zoos play an important role in protecting endangered species.
    • C In this essay I will first write about the advantages of zoos, then about the disadvantages, and at the end I will give my opinion.
    • D Zoos should be closed. Animals suffer. People should not go there.
     ✔ B
    2 Question: Do the advantages of working from home outweigh the disadvantages? Which introduction is best?
    • A It is true that more people are now working from home. While I accept that this has some drawbacks, I believe that the advantages are more significant.
    • B Working from home has advantages and disadvantages.
    • C Since the beginning of time, humans have worked in many different places, and today technology is changing everything in our modern world.
    • D I think working from home is good and bad at the same time.
     ✔ A
    3 Question: Traffic congestion — causes and solutions. Which introduction is best?
    • A Traffic is bad. There are a lot of cars.
    • B I strongly agree that traffic congestion is a problem.
    • C It is true that many cities are affected by heavy traffic. There are several reasons for this problem, but governments could take a number of steps to reduce it.
    • D In my opinion, the advantages of traffic outweigh the disadvantages.
     ✔ C
    4 In an agree / disagree essay, what is wrong with a paragraph that starts "Some people believe… Other people believe…"?
    • A It turns the essay into a 'discuss both views' essay and hides your own opinion.
    • B It is too short.
    • C It uses informal language.
    • D Nothing is wrong with it.
     ✔ A
    5 What should a conclusion be, according to Simon?
    • A One sentence that repeats your answer to the question.
    • B A long paragraph with new ideas.
    • C A list of all the examples you used.
    • D It is not necessary.
     ✔ A
    6 Which sentence is the best topic sentence for a paragraph about the drawbacks of online courses?
    • A For example, my friend did an online course last year.
    • B The main drawback of online university courses is that there is less direct interaction.
    • C There are many things to say about this.
    • D Online courses, which are becoming more and more popular all over the world in every country, have some problems and also some good points.
     ✔ B

    Упражнение 10. Правила Simon для Task 2

    Верно или неверно?

    Decide whether each statement is TRUE or FALSE.

    1 When the question asks for your opinion, you can use "I believe" and "in my opinion". ✔ TRUE
    2 In an agree / disagree essay, you should write one paragraph about what other people think. ✔ FALSE
    3 If you partly agree, you can write one paragraph about each side, but from your own point of view. ✔ TRUE
    4 The introduction can be just two sentences: the topic in your own words and your answer. ✔ TRUE
    5 To get band 7 or higher, you need passives and conditionals in every paragraph. ✔ FALSE
    6 The conclusion is a good place to introduce a new important argument. ✔ FALSE
    7 If you need more words, you can expand one of the examples in a main paragraph. ✔ TRUE
    8 Each main paragraph should begin with a short topic sentence. ✔ TRUE
    9 In a "discuss both views and give your opinion" essay, it is enough to give your opinion only in the conclusion. ✔ FALSE
    10 If you write about ten words per line, you can quickly estimate how many words you have written. ✔ TRUE

    Как работать с образцами

    У каждого вопроса Task 2 ниже есть образец уровня Band 9 по шаблону Simon: план (какой шаблон и что в каждом абзаце), сам текст, отдельная таблица полезной лексики с переводом (эти выражения подсвечены в тексте) и разбор. Порядок: 5 минут на план → 35 минут на эссе от руки или в редакторе без проверки орфографии → открой образец и сравни структуру, позицию и связки. Не заучивай тексты целиком: экзаменаторы замечают заготовки. Забирай шаблоны, идеи и выражения.

    Task 2 — недавно попадалось на экзамене (с датами)

    1. Museums and historical sites are mainly visited by tourists rather than local people. Why is this the case? What can be done to attract more local people? (24 окт и 3 ноя 2026 · causes + solutions)
      Образец (Band 9), 309 слов — план, лексика, разбор
      План: Шаблон Simon «причины + решения». Вступление (2 предложения): тема своими словами + короткий ответ на оба вопроса. Абзац 2 — причины: Firstly (место всегда рядом, визит откладывают) + пример; Secondly (музеи сделаны для туристов). Абзац 3 — решения, каждое отвечает на причину: скидки для жителей, вечерние часы, меняющиеся выставки. Вывод — одно предложение.

      It is true that famous museums and historical sites are often full of tourists, while the people who live nearby rarely visit them. There are several reasons for this, but I believe that museums could take a number of steps to attract more local visitors.

      There are two main reasons why local people tend to stay away from the attractions in their own cities. Firstly, residents often feel that there is no hurry to visit a place that is always on their doorstep. A tourist who is spending three days in Rome, for example, will make the Colosseum a priority, whereas a person who lives in Rome may keep postponing the visit for years. Secondly, many museums are designed mainly with tourists in mind. Their permanent exhibitions rarely change, their ticket prices are set at a level that foreign visitors are willing to pay, and they are usually open only during normal working hours. As a result, a local person who has seen the collection once has little reason to return.

      However, there are several measures that could encourage local people to visit museums more often. A simple solution would be to offer residents free or discounted entry, as many cities already do on certain days of the month. Museums could also open late one evening a week, so that people who work during the day would have the chance to visit. Finally, it is important to give local visitors a reason to come back. By organising temporary exhibitions, talks and family activities that change regularly, museums could turn themselves into lively community centres rather than places that people see only once.

      In conclusion, local people often ignore the museums in their area because they are always available and seem to be aimed at tourists, but lower prices, longer opening hours and changing exhibitions could help to change this.

    2. Some people think that languages should be taught in small classes, while others believe that the number of students in a class does not matter. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. (30 сен, 14 окт, 4 ноя 2026 · discussion)
      Образец (Band 9), 284 слов — план, лексика, разбор
      План: Шаблон Simon «discuss both views + opinion». Вступление: People have different views about… + своя позиция (маленькие группы лучше). Абзац 2 — чужая точка зрения: учитель важнее размера группы; технологии дают практику вне класса. Абзац 3 — моя точка зрения (вторым абзацем!): язык = говорение, обратная связь, личный подход, личный пример. Вывод.

      People have different views about whether the size of a class affects how well students learn a foreign language. While some argue that class size is not important, I believe that languages are best taught in small groups.

      On the one hand, there are some reasons why people believe that the number of students in a language class does not matter. Firstly, the quality of the teacher is arguably more important than the size of the group. A skilled and enthusiastic teacher can keep a class of thirty students engaged, while a poor teacher may fail to motivate even five learners. Secondly, modern technology allows students to practise outside the classroom. For example, learners can use language apps, watch films with subtitles or chat online with native speakers, so they do not depend entirely on the time they spend speaking in class.

      On the other hand, I would argue that small classes are far more effective, because learning a language requires a great deal of speaking practice. In a group of eight students, each learner has the opportunity to speak regularly, ask questions and receive feedback on their mistakes. In a class of thirty, by contrast, most students spend the lesson listening, and shy learners can easily avoid speaking at all. Furthermore, a teacher with a small group can identify the specific weaknesses of each student and adapt the lesson accordingly. In my own experience, the English lessons that helped me most were those in which I was forced to speak and was corrected immediately.

      In conclusion, although a good teacher and modern technology can help any class, I believe that smaller groups give students a much better chance of learning a language successfully.

    3. The extinction of some animal species, as happened with dinosaurs and dodos, is a natural process, and people should not try to prevent it. To what extent do you agree or disagree? (7 сен, 2 ноя 2026 · opinion)
      Образец (Band 9), 285 слов — план, лексика, разбор
      План: Шаблон Simon «completely disagree». Вступление: перефраз + I completely disagree. Абзац 2 — первая причина: сегодняшнее вымирание вызвано людьми, а не природой (динозавры vs додо). Абзац 3 — вторая причина: защита видов в наших интересах (экосистемы, пчёлы, лекарства, будущие поколения). Вывод. Абзаца «что думают другие» нет — Simon прямо так советует.

      Some people argue that the extinction of animal species is a natural process, and that humans should therefore not try to stop it. I completely disagree with this view.

      In my opinion, it is wrong to compare the current loss of species with the disappearance of the dinosaurs. It is true that extinction has always been part of the history of life on Earth, but the dinosaurs died out as a result of natural events over which nobody had any control. Today, by contrast, most species are threatened because of human activity. Forests are being cut down, rivers and oceans are being polluted, and animals such as rhinos and tigers are hunted for profit. The dodo itself disappeared shortly after sailors arrived on its island and began killing it for food. Since humans are largely responsible for this crisis, I believe that we have a duty to try to solve it.

      I also believe that protecting endangered species is in our own interest. Every species plays a role in its ecosystem, and the loss of one can have serious effects on many others. For example, bees pollinate a large proportion of the crops that we eat, so a sharp decline in bee populations would threaten our food supply. Furthermore, many medicines have been developed from plants and animals, and it would be foolish to destroy species before we understand their potential value. Finally, wildlife is a source of wonder and enjoyment for millions of people, and future generations deserve the chance to see these animals.

      In conclusion, I do not accept that extinction is simply a natural process in today's world, and I believe that we should do everything we can to protect endangered species.

    4. Because people around the world watch the same films and television programmes and use the same media, countries are becoming more and more alike. Do the advantages of this outweigh the disadvantages? (21 авг, 28 окт 2026 · advantages / disadvantages)
      Образец (Band 9), 265 слов — план, лексика, разбор
      План: Шаблон Simon «advantages vs disadvantages» (как его эссе про видеоигры). Вступление: факт + While I accept that…, I believe… (недостатков больше). Абзац 2 — плюсы (On the one hand): общие темы, языки, качественные программы. Абзац 3 — минусы (However, I would argue that these benefits are outweighed by the drawbacks): потеря местной культуры, местное кино не может конкурировать. Вывод.

      It is true that people all over the world now watch the same films, follow the same television series and use the same social media platforms. While I accept that this trend has some benefits, I believe that the disadvantages are more significant.

      On the one hand, global media can bring people from different countries closer together. When teenagers in Brazil, Korea and Germany watch the same series, they have something in common to talk about, and this can help to create friendships across borders. Shared media also makes it easier for people to learn foreign languages, especially English, because they are exposed to it every day. In addition, international film and television companies have the money to produce high-quality entertainment, so viewers in smaller countries have access to programmes that their own industries could never afford to make.

      However, I would argue that these benefits are outweighed by the drawbacks. The main problem is that local cultures are gradually being replaced by a single global culture that is largely produced in the USA. If young people grow up watching only Hollywood films, they may lose interest in their own country's stories, music and traditions. As a result, the rich variety of cultures that makes travel and international contact so interesting could slowly disappear. Furthermore, local film industries often cannot compete with the huge budgets of international studios, and many talented writers and directors may therefore struggle to find work.

      In conclusion, it seems to me that the loss of cultural diversity is a greater price to pay than the benefits of shared global entertainment.

    5. In many countries, fewer and fewer people use bicycles as a means of transport. Why is this happening? What could be done to encourage people to cycle more? (27 авг, 21 окт 2026 · causes + solutions)
      Образец (Band 9), 274 слов — план, лексика, разбор
      План: Шаблон Simon «причины + решения» (как его эссе про жизнь в городах). Вступление: факт + ответ на оба вопроса. Абзац 2 — There are various reasons why…: опасно ездить, большие расстояния, машины стали доступнее. Абзац 3 — However, there are several steps that could be taken…: велодорожки (пример Копенгагена), прокат велосипедов, душ на работе, дорогая парковка. Вывод.

      It is true that cycling has become less popular as a means of transport in many countries. There are several reasons for this trend, but I believe that governments and local authorities could do a lot to encourage people to cycle more.

      There are various reasons why fewer people choose to travel by bicycle. Firstly, many people feel that cycling in city traffic is dangerous. On busy roads without separate cycle lanes, cyclists have to share space with cars, buses and lorries, and accidents can have serious consequences. Secondly, cities have grown larger, and people often live a long way from their workplaces. A journey of twenty kilometres is simply too long for most people to cycle every day, especially in hot or rainy weather. Finally, cars have become more affordable, and for many families a car is now seen as a symbol of success and comfort.

      However, there are several steps that could be taken to make cycling more attractive. The most important measure would be to build a network of safe cycle lanes that are physically separated from motor traffic. Cities such as Copenhagen and Amsterdam have shown that when cycling feels safe, large numbers of people choose to do it. Governments could also introduce bike-sharing schemes, so that people can rent a bicycle cheaply for short journeys, and employers could be encouraged to provide showers and secure parking for staff who cycle to work. Finally, higher parking charges in city centres would make driving less convenient.

      In conclusion, safety concerns, longer journeys and cheaper cars have all reduced the popularity of cycling, but better infrastructure and incentives could reverse this trend.

    6. Some people believe that the best way to improve road safety is to raise the minimum legal age for driving cars and motorbikes. To what extent do you agree or disagree? (31 июл 2026 · opinion)
      Образец (Band 9), 284 слов — план, лексика, разбор
      План: Шаблон Simon «partly agree». Вступление: перефраз + While I agree that…, I do not believe that… Абзац 2 — On the one hand, I accept that…: молодые водители чаще попадают в аварии. Абзац 3 — On the other hand, I believe…: дело в опыте, а не возрасте; лучше обучение и строгие меры; трудности для сельской молодёжи. Вывод.

      Some people believe that increasing the minimum age for driving cars and motorbikes would be the most effective way to make roads safer. While I agree that young drivers are often a danger on the roads, I do not believe that raising the driving age is the best solution.

      On the one hand, I accept that there are good arguments for raising the legal driving age. Statistics in many countries show that drivers under the age of twenty-five are involved in a disproportionate number of serious accidents. Young drivers tend to lack experience, and some of them take unnecessary risks, such as driving too fast or using their phones at the wheel. If the minimum age were raised from seventeen or eighteen to twenty-one, for example, new drivers might be more mature and responsible.

      On the other hand, I believe that other measures would be far more effective. Firstly, the problem is inexperience rather than age itself, and a twenty-one-year-old beginner may make the same mistakes as an eighteen-year-old. It would therefore be better to make driving tests more demanding and to require new drivers to complete a longer period of supervised practice. Secondly, many accidents are caused by older drivers who break the rules, for instance by drinking and driving. Strict punishments, speed cameras and better road design would reduce these accidents for drivers of all ages. Finally, raising the driving age would cause real hardship for young people in rural areas who depend on a car to get to work or college.

      In conclusion, although young drivers are a genuine concern, I believe that better training and stricter enforcement of the law would improve road safety more than a higher driving age.

    Task 2 — банк актуальных вопросов 2026 по темам

    Education

    1. Some people think that the values children learn from their family and parents have more influence on their future success than the knowledge and skills they learn at school. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
      Образец (Band 9), 279 слов — план, лексика, разбор
      План: Шаблон Simon «completely agree». Вступление: перефраз + I completely agree. Абзац 2 — ценности из семьи формируют поведение во взрослой жизни (честность, упорство) + пример. Абзац 3 — признаю роль школы (It is true that…), но опровергаю: знания забываются, а отношение к учёбе тоже идёт из семьи. Вывод.

      Some people argue that the values children learn from their parents have a greater effect on their future success than the knowledge and skills they acquire at school. I completely agree with this view.

      In my opinion, the qualities that lead to success in adult life are mainly learned at home. Parents teach their children basic values such as honesty, hard work, patience and respect for others, and these values shape the way people behave throughout their lives. For example, a child who sees his or her parents working hard and keeping their promises is likely to become a reliable employee and a trustworthy business partner. Similarly, children who are encouraged by their families to keep trying after a failure develop the determination that is needed in any career. These personal qualities often matter more to employers than academic grades.

      It is true that schools provide important knowledge and skills, but I would argue that their influence is more limited. Much of what students learn in lessons, such as the details of history or advanced mathematics, is quickly forgotten, and many people end up working in fields that have little connection with what they studied. Furthermore, the attitude that a child brings to school depends largely on the family. Pupils who have been taught at home to value education are far more likely to listen, complete their homework and make use of the opportunities that school offers. In other words, even academic success often has its roots in family values.

      In conclusion, I believe that the values that children learn from their parents play a more important role in their future success than the knowledge they gain at school.

    2. Since higher education mainly benefits individuals rather than society, students should pay the full cost of their university studies. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
      Образец (Band 9), 267 слов — план, лексика, разбор
      План: Шаблон Simon «completely disagree» (как его эссе про налоги и частные школы). Вступление: перефраз + Personally, I completely disagree. Абзац 2 — от образования выигрывает всё общество (врачи, учителя, налоги выпускников). Абзац 3 — полная оплата несправедлива: только богатые смогут учиться, долги; лучшая система — смешанная. Вывод.

      Some people believe that university students should pay the full cost of their education because they are the main beneficiaries of it. Personally, I completely disagree with this view.

      It is true that a university degree brings personal benefits. Graduates usually earn higher salaries than people with fewer qualifications, and they often have access to more interesting and secure jobs. However, I believe that it is wrong to say that higher education mainly benefits individuals. Society as a whole gains a great deal from having a well-educated population. Doctors, teachers, engineers and scientists all need university training, and without them our hospitals, schools and industries could not function. In addition, graduates pay more income tax because of their higher salaries, so the state recovers much of the money that it spends on their education.

      Furthermore, making students pay the full cost of their studies would be unfair. If university fees were extremely high, only young people from wealthy families would be able to afford a degree, while talented students from poorer backgrounds would be excluded. This would waste a huge amount of potential talent, and it would increase inequality in society. Some students might be able to take out loans, but many would be put off by the prospect of starting their working lives with enormous debts. In my view, the best system is one in which governments cover most of the cost of higher education, and students make a reasonable contribution.

      In conclusion, I do not believe that students should have to pay the full cost of university, because higher education benefits the whole of society.

    3. Competition for university places is increasing in many countries. Why is this happening? Is it a positive or negative development?
      Образец (Band 9), 281 слов — план, лексика, разбор
      План: Шаблон Simon «причины + оценка» (как его эссе про отцов-домохозяев). Вступление: факт + There could be several reasons for this, and… (в целом негативно). Абзац 2 — причины: больше выпускников школ, диплом нужен почти везде, конкуренция с иностранцами. Абзац 3 — In my view…: стресс, репетиторы, преимущество богатых. Вывод.

      It is true that it has become much harder to win a place at a good university in many countries. There could be several reasons for this, and in my opinion it is a largely negative development.

      In recent years, the demand for higher education has grown faster than the number of university places. Firstly, populations in many developing countries are young and growing, so each year there are more school leavers who want to study. Secondly, a degree is now seen as essential for most well-paid jobs. Positions that once required only a school certificate, such as nursing or office management, now often ask for a bachelor's degree, and parents therefore put great pressure on their children to go to university. Finally, the best universities attract applicants from all over the world, which means that local students must compete with talented candidates from abroad.

      In my view, this intense competition has more drawbacks than benefits. It is true that it may push some students to work harder and achieve higher grades. However, it also places enormous stress on teenagers, many of whom spend their final years at school preparing for entrance exams instead of developing other interests. In some countries, families spend huge sums on private tutors, which gives wealthy students an unfair advantage over those from poorer homes. As a result, university places may increasingly go to the richest rather than the most talented applicants, and many capable young people may be left without the opportunity to study at all.

      In conclusion, the rising demand for degrees and the global nature of higher education have made university places more competitive, and I believe that this trend is mainly harmful.

    4. Some people think young people should go to university after school, while others believe they should start work straight away. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
      Образец (Band 9), 271 слов — план, лексика, разбор
      План: Шаблон Simon «discuss both views». Вступление: дилемма выпускника + While/Although…, I believe… (университет лучше для большинства). Абзац 2 — On the one hand, there are several reasons why some people prefer…: деньги, опыт на работе. Абзац 3 — On the other hand, I believe…: диплом обязателен для многих профессий, универсальные навыки, переобучение. Вывод.

      When they leave school, young people have to decide whether to continue their education or to look for a job immediately. Although starting work early suits some school leavers, I believe that most young people benefit more from going to university.

      On the one hand, there are several reasons why some people prefer to enter the job market straight after school. The most obvious one is financial. University courses are expensive, and many graduates spend years paying back their student loans, whereas a young person who starts work at eighteen can begin saving money immediately. In addition, practical experience is highly valued in many industries. In fields such as construction, hospitality and even software development, a motivated eighteen-year-old who learns on the job may be earning a good salary and holding a responsible position by the time his or her friends graduate.

      On the other hand, I believe that higher education offers greater long-term advantages. Firstly, a degree remains the minimum requirement for many professions, including medicine, law, engineering and teaching, so a person who skips university may close the door to these careers. Secondly, university develops skills that go beyond any single job, such as independent research, critical thinking and the ability to write clearly. These skills become more important as people move into senior roles. Finally, the job market is changing quickly, and graduates are generally better prepared to retrain when their first career disappears or changes.

      In conclusion, starting work after school can be the right choice for some people, but in my opinion going to university gives most young people a stronger foundation for their future careers.

    5. Children can learn effectively by watching television, so they should be encouraged to watch it both at home and at school. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
      Образец (Band 9), 261 слов — план, лексика, разбор
      План: Шаблон Simon «disagree с уступкой». Вступление: It is true that… However, I do not agree… Абзац 2 — уступка: хорошие документальные фильмы полезны, но только выбранные с конкретной целью. Абзац 3 — In my opinion…: дети и так у экранов, ТВ пассивно, родителям будет труднее ограничивать. Вывод.

      It is true that some television programmes can teach children a great deal about the world. However, I do not agree that children should be encouraged to watch more television, either at home or at school.

      I accept that television can be a useful educational tool in certain situations. Well-made documentaries can show children wild animals in their natural habitats, explain how volcanoes work or bring historical events to life in a way that a textbook cannot. For young children, programmes designed to teach letters and numbers can also be helpful. In a classroom, a short video clip can introduce a new topic and make a lesson more memorable. However, the key point is that these benefits come from carefully chosen programmes used for a specific purpose, not from watching television in general.

      In my opinion, encouraging children to watch television would do more harm than good. Most children already spend several hours a day in front of screens, and they need more time for physical activity, reading and playing with friends, not less. Watching television is also a passive activity. Children learn most effectively when they ask questions, solve problems and practise new skills themselves, and a teacher who relies on videos may miss the chance to involve pupils actively in the lesson. Finally, if children are told that watching TV is educational, parents may find it even harder to limit their screen time at home.

      In conclusion, although selected programmes can support learning, I believe that children should be encouraged to spend less time watching television rather than more.
