    Part 14–5 минВопросы о тебе: работа/учёба, дом + 2 бытовые темы2–3 предложения: ответ + причина + пример
    Part 23–4 минКарточка: 1 мин на подготовку, 1–2 мин монологГовори до остановки экзаменатора; иди по пунктам карточки
    Part 34–5 минАбстрактные вопросы по теме карточки4–6 предложений: мнение → причина → пример → оговорка

    Критерии (по 25%): Fluency & Coherence · Lexical Resource · Grammatical Range & Accuracy · Pronunciation.

    Полезные фразы

    • Выиграть время: That's an interesting question. / I've never really thought about it, but… / Let me think…
    • Мнение: As far as I'm concerned… / I'd say that… / From my point of view… / I tend to think…
    • Пример: For instance… / Take my brother, for example… / A good example of this is…
    • Сравнение прошлого и настоящего: Compared with the past… / People used to…, whereas nowadays… / It's much more common now to…
    • Оговорка: Having said that… / It depends on… / On the other hand… / That's not always the case, though.
    • Part 2, начало и конец: I'd like to talk about… / The reason I chose this is… / All in all, it was… / Looking back, I think…
    • Если не понял: Sorry, could you repeat that, please? / Do you mean…?

    Схема ответа Part 2 на 2 минуты

    1. 10 сек — что/кто это (I'd like to tell you about…)
    2. 30 сек — фон: когда, где, как ты об этом узнал
    3. 50 сек — детали: что происходило (Past Simple / Past Continuous / Past Perfect)
    4. 30 сек — чувства и почему это важно; что изменилось (If I hadn't…, I would never have…)

    Part 1 — темы сентября–декабря 2026 с ответами

    Сначала ответь на вопросы сам вслух, потом открой тему и сравни. Ответы написаны на уровень Band 8: 2–3 предложения, причина и деталь. Не заучивай их — замени факты на свои (город, учёба, семья), а конструкции и лексику забирай.

    Обязательные темы (одна из них будет всегда)

    Work or Study. Are you working or studying? · Why did you choose your subject? · Do you enjoy it? · Do you prefer studying in the morning or afternoon? · What technology do you use when studying?

    Are you working or studying?
    I'm a second-year student at a university in Tashkent, majoring in economics. I also do a bit of private tutoring at weekends, so I suppose I'm doing a little of both.

    Why did you choose your subject?
    Mainly because I've always been good with numbers, and economics seemed more practical than pure maths. I also liked the idea that it explains everyday things, like why prices go up.

    Do you enjoy it?
    On the whole, yes. Some of the theory is quite dry, to be honest, but I really enjoy the seminars where we argue about real cases.

    Do you prefer studying in the morning or afternoon?
    Definitely the morning. My mind is much fresher before lunch, whereas by mid-afternoon I find myself reading the same paragraph three times.

    What technology do you use when studying?
    Mostly my laptop, for writing essays and looking things up. I also use a flashcard app on my phone to revise vocabulary whenever I'm on the bus.

    Лексика: major in — специализироваться на; dry — сухой, скучный; on the whole — в целом; look things up — искать информацию; revise — повторять
    Разбор: Обрати внимание на приём «ответ + причина + деталь». Фразы to be honest, I suppose, on the whole делают речь естественной и работают на Fluency.
    Home and Accommodation. Do you live in a house or an apartment? · Which part of your home do you like the most? · Do you plan to live there for a long time? · Would you prefer a house or an apartment in the future?

    Do you live in a house or an apartment?
    I live in an apartment on the fourth floor of a fairly old building. It's nothing fancy, but it's bright and it's only ten minutes from the metro.

    Which part of your home do you like the most?
    Probably the balcony. It's tiny, but my mother has filled it with plants, and it's the perfect spot for a cup of tea in the evening.

    Do you plan to live there for a long time?
    For the next couple of years, yes, until I graduate. After that I'd like to move out and get a place of my own.

    Would you prefer a house or an apartment in the future?
    Ideally a house with a small garden, because I'd love to have a bit of outdoor space. Realistically, though, an apartment is far more affordable in a big city.

    Лексика: nothing fancy — ничего особенного; the perfect spot — идеальное место; a place of my own — своё жильё; affordable — доступный по цене
    Разбор: Контраст ideally… realistically, though… показывает умение сравнивать и строить сложные предложения.
    Hometown. Where is your hometown? · Do you like it? · What is it famous for? · Has it changed much?

    Where is your hometown?
    I come from Samarkand, which is in the central part of Uzbekistan, about three hundred kilometres from the capital.

    Do you like it?
    I love it. It's big enough to have everything you need, yet it still has a relaxed pace of life that you don't get in the capital.

    What is it famous for?
    It's best known for its historic architecture, especially Registan Square with its blue-tiled buildings. It's also famous for its bread, which people say tastes different from anywhere else.

    Has it changed much?
    Quite a lot, actually. In the last ten years lots of hotels and cafés have opened because of tourism, and the old centre has been restored. Some people feel it's lost a little of its character, though.

    Лексика: pace of life — ритм жизни; be best known for — больше всего известен; blue-tiled — с голубой плиткой; restore — реставрировать; lose its character — утратить своеобразие
    Разбор: Present Perfect (have opened, has been restored, it's lost) — стандартный способ говорить об изменениях. Подставь свой город.
    The Area You Live In. Do you like the area where you live? · Do you know your neighbours? · Is your area noisy? · Has the area changed recently?

    Do you like the area where you live?
    Yes, on the whole. It's a residential neighbourhood with lots of trees, and there's a market within walking distance, which is really convenient.

    Do you know your neighbours?
    I know the ones on our floor pretty well. We exchange food on holidays, and the lady next door sometimes looks after our cat when we're away.

    Is your area noisy?
    Not particularly, apart from rush hour, when you can hear the traffic from the main road. At night it's surprisingly peaceful.

    Has the area changed recently?
    A little. A couple of new apartment blocks have gone up, so it's more crowded than it used to be, and parking has become a real headache.

    Лексика: residential — жилой; within walking distance — в пешей доступности; look after — присматривать; go up — вырастать (о зданиях); a real headache — настоящая головная боль
    The City You Live In. What city do you live in? · Do you like living there? · Would you recommend your city to others?

    What city do you live in?
    I live in Tashkent, the capital. It's by far the largest city in the country, with around three million people.

    Do you like living there?
    Most of the time, yes. There's always something going on, and the public transport is decent. The only thing I can't stand is the heat in July.

    Would you recommend your city to others?
    I would, especially to people who enjoy food and history. I'd tell them to come in spring or autumn, though, when the weather is at its best.

    Лексика: by far — безусловно, намного; there's always something going on — всегда что-то происходит; can't stand — не выношу; at its best — в лучшем виде

    Сменные темы сезона

    Teacher. Do you have a favourite teacher? · How did your favourite teacher help you? · Are you still in touch with your old teachers? · Would you like to become a teacher?

    Do you have a favourite teacher?
    Yes, my English teacher from secondary school. She was strict, but she had a great sense of humour, and her lessons never felt like a chore.

    How did your favourite teacher help you?
    She was the first person who told me I had a talent for languages. That gave me a real boost, and she also lent me books to read outside class.

    Are you still in touch with your old teachers?
    Only with her, really. I send her a message on Teachers' Day every year, and she always asks how my studies are going.

    Would you like to become a teacher?
    Probably not full-time. I enjoy explaining things, but I don't think I'd have the patience to deal with thirty teenagers every day.

    Лексика: feel like a chore — быть в тягость; give someone a boost — придать уверенности; be in touch with — поддерживать связь; have the patience to — хватать терпения
    Social Media. When did you start using social media? · Do you think you spend too much time on it? · What do people usually do on social media? · Have you ever posted anything online?

    When did you start using social media?
    When I was about thirteen, I think. Everyone in my class was on it, so I joined mainly so I wouldn't feel left out.

    Do you think you spend too much time on it?
    Honestly, yes. I pick up my phone to check one message, and before I know it half an hour has gone. I've started setting a daily limit to cut down.

    What do people usually do on social media?
    Mostly they scroll through short videos and photos, keep up with friends, and follow the news. A lot of small businesses use it to advertise as well.

    Have you ever posted anything online?
    Yes, but not very often. I occasionally share photos from trips, but I'm quite a private person, so I think twice before posting.

    Лексика: feel left out — чувствовать себя в стороне; before I know it — не успеваю оглянуться; cut down — сократить; keep up with — быть в курсе; think twice — хорошенько подумать
    Music. Do you like music? · What kind of music do you enjoy? · Do you prefer happy or sad music? · Does happy music make you excited?

    Do you like music?
    Very much. I listen to it practically all day, on the way to university, while cooking, even when I'm studying.

    What kind of music do you enjoy?
    My taste is fairly broad. I'm into indie rock at the moment, but I also enjoy traditional music at weddings and family gatherings.

    Do you prefer happy or sad music?
    It depends on my mood, but I lean towards slower, slightly melancholy songs. I find they help me unwind after a long day.

    Does happy music make you excited?
    It does, actually. If an upbeat song comes on while I'm cleaning, I get the job done twice as fast.

    Лексика: be into — увлекаться; lean towards — склоняться к; unwind — расслабляться; upbeat — бодрый, весёлый
    Singing. Do you like singing? · Did you sing as a child? · Do you sing in the car?

    Do you like singing?
    I do, although I'm not sure the people around me enjoy it. I can't really hold a tune, so I mostly sing when nobody's listening.

    Did you sing as a child?
    Yes, I was in the school choir for a couple of years. We used to perform at holiday concerts, and I remember being terribly nervous on stage.

    Do you sing in the car?
    All the time, especially on long journeys with friends. We put on old pop songs and sing along at the top of our voices.

    Лексика: hold a tune — попадать в ноты; choir — хор; sing along — подпевать; at the top of our voices — во весь голос
    Headphones. Do you use headphones often? · Are headphones useful? · When should people avoid using headphones?

    Do you use headphones often?
    Every single day. I put them on as soon as I leave the house, and I'd feel lost without them on public transport.

    Are headphones useful?
    Extremely. They let you listen to whatever you like without disturbing anyone, and noise-cancelling ones are a lifesaver if you need to concentrate in a noisy place.

    When should people avoid using headphones?
    When they're crossing the road or cycling, because you need to hear the traffic. I also think it's rude to keep them in while someone is talking to you.

    Лексика: feel lost without — как без рук; noise-cancelling — с шумоподавлением; a lifesaver — спасение; keep them in — не вынимать
    Tidiness. Do you like keeping things tidy? · Were you tidy as a child? · Are you a tidy person now?

    Do you like keeping things tidy?
    I do. I can't concentrate if my desk is a mess, so I usually spend five minutes clearing up before I start working.

    Were you tidy as a child?
    Not at all. My room was a disaster, and my mother was constantly telling me to pick my clothes up off the floor.

    Are you a tidy person now?
    Much more than I used to be. Sharing a room at university taught me that if you don't put things away, you'll never find them again.

    Лексика: a mess — беспорядок; clear up — прибираться; a disaster — катастрофа; put things away — убирать вещи на место
    Разбор: used to be / was constantly telling — хорошие формы для сравнения прошлого и настоящего.
    Websites. What kinds of websites do you visit? · What is your favourite website? · Have websites changed in recent years? · Would you like to have your own website?

    What kinds of websites do you visit?
    Mainly news sites and educational ones. I also spend a fair amount of time on online shops, comparing prices before I buy anything.

    What is your favourite website?
    Probably a site with free online courses. I've taken a couple of statistics courses there, and the lectures are easier to follow than some at my university.

    Have websites changed in recent years?
    Definitely. They load much faster and are designed for phones first. The downside is that almost every page now asks you to accept cookies or subscribe to something.

    Would you like to have your own website?
    Maybe one day, as a kind of online portfolio. It would be a good way to show employers what I've done.

    Лексика: a fair amount of — довольно много; easy to follow — легко воспринимать; the downside — минус; subscribe — подписаться
    Computers and Tablets. Do you use a computer regularly? · Do you prefer computers or tablets? · When did you first start using computers?

    Do you use a computer regularly?
    Every day. All my coursework is done on my laptop, and I use it for video calls with relatives who live abroad.

    Do you prefer computers or tablets?
    Computers, without a doubt. A tablet is fine for watching films, but typing a long essay on a touchscreen would drive me mad.

    When did you first start using computers?
    I must have been about seven. We had an old desktop at home, and I mostly used it to play simple games and draw pictures.

    Лексика: coursework — учебные задания; without a doubt — без сомнения; drive me mad — свести с ума; I must have been — мне было, наверное
    Watches. Do you wear a watch? · Have you ever received a watch as a gift? · Why do people wear expensive watches? · Is wearing a watch still important?

    Do you wear a watch?
    I used to, but I stopped a couple of years ago because I check the time on my phone anyway. I only put one on for formal occasions.

    Have you ever received a watch as a gift?
    Yes, my grandfather gave me one when I finished school. It isn't expensive, but it has huge sentimental value for me.

    Why do people wear expensive watches?
    Mostly as a status symbol, I'd say. A luxury watch tells the world you've been successful. Some people also see them as an investment.

    Is wearing a watch still important?
    Less than it used to be. Having said that, smartwatches have made them popular again, since they track your health as well as tell the time.

    Лексика: sentimental value — памятная ценность; status symbol — символ статуса; having said that — тем не менее; track — отслеживать
    Shopping. Do you enjoy shopping? · How often do you go shopping? · Do you prefer online or in-store shopping? · Do you compare prices?

    Do you enjoy shopping?
    It depends what for. I quite enjoy browsing in bookshops, but shopping for clothes wears me out after about an hour.

    How often do you go shopping?
    For groceries, two or three times a week. For anything else, only when I really need something, maybe once a month.

    Do you prefer online or in-store shopping?
    Online for electronics, because it's easier to compare. For shoes and clothes I'd rather go to a shop, since I like to try things on first.

    Do you compare prices?
    Always. I'm on a student budget, so I check two or three places before buying anything that costs more than a meal.

    Лексика: browse — рассматривать товары; wear me out — утомлять; try things on — примерять; be on a budget — жить экономно
    Street Markets. Do you visit street markets? · What do people normally buy there? · Do you prefer street markets or shopping malls?

    Do you visit street markets?
    Quite often. There's a big bazaar near my home, and I go there most Sundays with my mother.

    What do people normally buy there?
    Mainly fresh produce, like fruit, vegetables, nuts and spices. You can also find fresh bread, and the stallholders usually let you taste before you buy.

    Do you prefer street markets or shopping malls?
    For food, markets every time, because everything is fresher and you can bargain. Malls are more comfortable in summer, though, thanks to the air conditioning.

    Лексика: fresh produce — свежие овощи и фрукты; stallholder — торговец на рынке; bargain — торговаться; every time — однозначно
    Clothing. What kind of clothes do you normally wear? · Do you prefer casual or smart clothes? · Do you like wearing T-shirts? · Do you spend a long time choosing clothes?

    What kind of clothes do you normally wear?
    Mostly jeans and a plain shirt or hoodie. I go for comfort rather than fashion, to be honest.

    Do you prefer casual or smart clothes?
    Casual, definitely. I do own a suit, but it only comes out for weddings and job interviews.

    Do you like wearing T-shirts?
    Yes, I practically live in them in summer. I prefer plain ones without big logos.

    Do you spend a long time choosing clothes?
    Hardly any. I decide what to wear in about a minute, mainly because most of my clothes go with each other.

    Лексика: go for — выбирать; live in — не вылезать из; plain — однотонный; go with — сочетаться
    Cars. Did you enjoy travelling by car as a child? · What type of cars do you like? · Do you prefer being a driver or a passenger? · What do you do in a traffic jam?

    Did you enjoy travelling by car as a child?
    I loved it. We used to drive to my grandparents' village, and I'd spend the whole journey with my face pressed against the window.

    What type of cars do you like?
    Small, economical ones. I've never understood the appeal of huge cars that are impossible to park.

    Do you prefer being a driver or a passenger?
    A passenger, at least for now. I only passed my test last year, and driving in city traffic still makes me tense.

    What do you do in a traffic jam?
    I usually put on a podcast and try to stay calm. There's no point getting annoyed about something you can't change.

    Лексика: appeal — привлекательность; pass my test — сдать на права; make me tense — напрягать; there's no point — нет смысла
    Разбор: used to drive / I'd spend — would и used to для привычных действий в прошлом.
    Parks. Did you enjoy going to parks as a child? · Do you still visit parks? · Should cities have more parks?

    Did you enjoy going to parks as a child?
    Very much. There was a park with an old Ferris wheel near our home, and going there was the highlight of my week.

    Do you still visit parks?
    Yes, though for different reasons. Nowadays I go jogging there in the mornings, or sit on a bench with a book.

    Should cities have more parks?
    Absolutely. They give people somewhere to relax for free, and trees make a real difference to the air quality and the temperature in summer.

    Лексика: the highlight of — лучший момент; go jogging — бегать трусцой; make a real difference — заметно влиять
    Science. Do you like science? · Which area of science interests you most? · Do you watch science programmes?

    Do you like science?
    I do, although I was never a star pupil in physics. I find it fascinating to learn how things actually work.

    Which area of science interests you most?
    Probably biology, especially anything to do with the brain. It amazes me how little we still know about it.

    Do you watch science programmes?
    Fairly regularly. I follow a couple of channels that explain complicated ideas in ten minutes, which suits my attention span.

    Лексика: star pupil — лучший ученик; anything to do with — всё, что связано с; it amazes me — меня поражает; attention span — способность удерживать внимание
    Outer Space and Stars. Have you learned about space before? · Would you like to learn more about it? · Do you enjoy science-fiction films? · Would you like to travel into space?

    Have you learned about space before?
    A little, at school. We had one term of astronomy, and I still remember the order of the planets.

    Would you like to learn more about it?
    Definitely. I'd especially like to understand black holes, because every explanation I've read has left me more confused.

    Do you enjoy science-fiction films?
    I do, as long as the story is good. I prefer the thoughtful ones about space travel to the ones that are just explosions.

    Would you like to travel into space?
    In theory, yes. In practice, I get nervous on ordinary flights, so I'd probably let other people go first.

    Лексика: as long as — при условии, что; thoughtful — глубокий, умный; in theory… in practice — в теории… на практике
    History. Do you like history? · Did you like history at school? · Have you visited a historical museum? · When did you last read about history?

    Do you like history?
    Yes, more now than when I was younger. I've realised that you can't really understand the present without it.

    Did you like history at school?
    Not especially. It was mostly memorising dates, which bored me. I only started enjoying it when I read books on my own.

    Have you visited a historical museum?
    Several times. The most recent was the state history museum, where I was struck by a collection of coins from the Silk Road.

    When did you last read about history?
    Just last week, in fact. I read a long article about how tea spread around the world.

    Лексика: memorise — заучивать; on my own — самостоятельно; be struck by — быть поражённым; in fact — вообще-то
    Old Buildings. Are there old buildings in your city? · Should old buildings be protected? · Would you prefer an old or a modern home? · Is there an old building you'd like to visit?

    Are there old buildings in your city?
    Plenty. The old town has mosques and schools that are five or six hundred years old, and people still use some of them.

    Should old buildings be protected?
    Without question. Once they're gone, they're gone for ever, and they're a huge part of what makes a city unique.

    Would you prefer an old or a modern home?
    A modern one, if I'm honest. Old houses are charming, but I'd miss decent heating and fast internet.

    Is there an old building you'd like to visit?
    I'd love to see the Alhambra in Spain. I've seen so many photos of its courtyards that I want to find out if it's as beautiful in real life.

    Лексика: plenty — множество; without question — бесспорно; charming — очаровательный; in real life — вживую
    Feeling Bored. Do you often feel bored? · What kinds of things bore you? · What do you do when you're bored? · Did you find school boring?

    Do you often feel bored?
    Not very often. I've got quite a full timetable, so there isn't much room for boredom.

    What kinds of things bore you?
    Waiting, more than anything. Standing in a long queue at the bank with nothing to do drives me up the wall.

    What do you do when you're bored?
    I usually reach for my phone, I'm afraid. If I'm at home, I'll go for a walk or call a friend instead.

    Did you find school boring?
    Parts of it. Lessons where we just copied from the board were dull, but I enjoyed anything involving discussion.

    Лексика: there isn't much room for — почти нет места для; drive me up the wall — выводить из себя; reach for — тянуться к; dull — скучный
    Mirrors. Do you often look in the mirror? · Have you ever bought a mirror? · Do you carry a mirror? · Would you decorate a room with mirrors?

    Do you often look in the mirror?
    Just a couple of times a day, when I'm getting ready in the morning and before I go out.

    Have you ever bought a mirror?
    Yes, I bought a full-length one for my room last year, so I could check my outfit before leaving.

    Do you carry a mirror?
    No, I don't. If I need one, I just use the camera on my phone.

    Would you decorate a room with mirrors?
    I would, in moderation. A large mirror makes a small room look bigger and brighter, but too many would feel strange.

    Лексика: get ready — собираться; full-length — в полный рост; in moderation — в меру
    Jokes and Comedies. Are you good at telling jokes? · Do your friends like telling jokes? · Do you like watching comedy? · Are comedy shows popular in your country?

    Are you good at telling jokes?
    Not really. I always mess up the ending. I'm better at making funny comments in conversation.

    Do your friends like telling jokes?
    One of them does. He can keep a whole table laughing for an hour, and he never seems to run out of stories.

    Do you like watching comedy?
    Yes, especially stand-up. It's my favourite way to switch off after exams.

    Are comedy shows popular in your country?
    Very. There are comedy competitions on television that families watch together, and the best performers become real celebrities.

    Лексика: mess up — испортить; run out of — исчерпать; switch off — отключиться, отдохнуть
    Dream and Ambition. What was your childhood dream? · Has your dream changed? · What is your dream job? · Are you ambitious?

    What was your childhood dream?
    I wanted to be a pilot. I was fascinated by planes and used to draw them in all my notebooks.

    Has your dream changed?
    Completely. Once I found out how much physics was involved, I lost interest, and economics gradually took over.

    What is your dream job?
    Something in international development, ideally with an organisation that works on poverty. I'd like my work to have some purpose.

    Are you ambitious?
    I'd say so, but in a quiet way. I set myself goals and work steadily towards them, without needing to be the best in the room.

    Лексика: be fascinated by — быть увлечённым; take over — занять место; have a purpose — иметь смысл; work steadily towards — планомерно идти к
    Morning Routines. What do you do immediately after waking up? · Is breakfast important to you? · Do you like getting up early? · Has your morning routine changed?

    What do you do immediately after waking up?
    I'm ashamed to say I check my phone. Then I drink a glass of water and open the window.

    Is breakfast important to you?
    Very. I can't function without it. Usually it's just eggs, bread and tea, but I never skip it.

    Do you like getting up early?
    I like having got up early, if that makes sense. The first ten minutes are painful, but I love how long the day feels.

    Has your morning routine changed?
    Yes, since I started university. At school my mother woke me; now I rely on three alarms.

    Лексика: I'm ashamed to say — стыдно признаться; can't function — не могу нормально работать; skip — пропускать; rely on — полагаться на
    Evening Time. Do you prefer mornings or evenings? · What do you usually do in the evening? · Are your evenings different from when you were a child? · Are your weekend evenings different?

    Do you prefer mornings or evenings?
    Evenings. That's the only time of day that really belongs to me, when all my tasks are done.

    What do you usually do in the evening?
    I have dinner with my family, then either read or watch an episode of something. Twice a week I play football with friends.

    Are your evenings different from when you were a child?
    Very. Back then I'd be outside until it got dark; these days I'm mostly indoors in front of a screen.

    Are your weekend evenings different?
    They're more sociable. On Saturdays I usually meet friends at a café, and we lose track of time talking.

    Лексика: belong to — принадлежать; back then — в те времена; sociable — общительный; lose track of time — терять счёт времени
    Sports Programmes. Do you like watching sports programmes? · Do you prefer watching live sport? · Who do you normally watch sport with? · Have you watched a match in a stadium?

    Do you like watching sports programmes?
    Yes, mainly football. I try not to miss the big international matches.

    Do you prefer watching live sport?
    Definitely. If I already know the score, most of the excitement disappears.

    Who do you normally watch sport with?
    With my father and my uncle. They shout at the television as if the players could hear them, which is half the fun.

    Have you watched a match in a stadium?
    Just once, a national league game. The atmosphere was electric, far better than on television.

    Лексика: the score — счёт; half the fun — половина удовольствия; the atmosphere was electric — атмосфера была наэлектризована
    Films and Cinema. What types of films do you like? · How often do you watch films? · Do you prefer watching films at home or at the cinema? · Do you go to the cinema with friends?

    What types of films do you like?
    I'm a fan of thrillers and anything based on a true story. I'm not keen on horror, though.

    How often do you watch films?
    About once a week at home, usually on Friday night.

    Do you prefer watching films at home or at the cinema?
    At home for most films, since I can pause whenever I want. For big action films, though, nothing beats a cinema screen.

    Do you go to the cinema with friends?
    Yes, almost always. Half the pleasure is arguing about the film over tea afterwards.

    Лексика: be keen on — увлекаться; based on a true story — основан на реальных событиях; nothing beats — ничто не сравнится с
    Collecting Things. Do you collect anything? · Have you kept anything from childhood? · Why do people collect things?

    Do you collect anything?
    Not seriously, but I do keep the tickets from every concert and match I've been to.

    Have you kept anything from childhood?
    Yes, a box of toy cars. Most are scratched, but I can't bring myself to throw them away.

    Why do people collect things?
    I think it gives them a sense of achievement, completing a set. For others it's about nostalgia, holding on to a period of their lives.

    Лексика: can't bring myself to — рука не поднимается; a sense of achievement — чувство достижения; hold on to — держаться за, сохранять

    Part 2 и Part 3 — 50 cue cards сезона

    Тема карточки — из отчётов сезона; пункты «You should say» и вопросы Part 3 составлены в стандартном экзаменационном формате. Под каждой карточкой — образец ответа на 1,5–2 минуты, лексика с переводом, разбор (почему это Band 8) и ответы на вопросы Part 3. Порядок работы: 1 минута на заметки → 2 минуты говори под запись → открой образец и сравни.

    Как читать разбор: что даёт Band 8

    • Fluency & Coherence. Ответ идёт по пунктам карточки и связан словами: at first, after a while, on top of that, as for…, looking back. Есть вывод в конце.
    • Lexical Resource. Не «умные» слова, а точные сочетания: put into perspective, keep at it, take pride in. В каждом разборе выписано 5 таких выражений.
    • Grammar. Смешение времён (Past Perfect для предыстории, would для привычек), условные, пассив, придаточные. Ошибки допустимы, но редкие.
    • Pronunciation. Текст это не покажет: читай образец вслух, записывай себя и сравнивай ритм и ударения.
    • Part 3. Схема ответа: позиция → причина → пример или оговорка. 3–4 предложения, без личных историй — говори об обществе в целом.

    People

    1. Describe a person who is much older than you that you admire.NEW
    You should say:
    • who this person is
    • how you know them
    • what they have done in their life
    • and explain why you admire them
    Part 3:
    • What can young people learn from older generations?
    • Are old people respected enough in your country?
    • Why do some young people ignore advice from the elderly?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'd like to talk about my grandfather, who turned eighty-two this year. He spent his whole career as a railway engineer, and although he retired more than twenty years ago, he's still the busiest person in our family. What I admire most is the way he never stops learning. A few years ago he decided he wanted to video-call his relatives abroad, so he asked me to teach him how to use a smartphone. He wrote every step down in a little notebook, and within a month he was sending us voice messages and photos of his garden. He's also incredibly patient. When I was struggling with maths at school, he'd sit with me for hours and explain the same thing in five different ways without ever raising his voice. On top of that, he has lived through some really hard times, yet I've never heard him complain. Whenever I feel like giving up on something, I think of him, and it puts my own problems into perspective.

    Лексика: turn eighty-two — исполниться 82; never raise his voice — никогда не повышать голос; live through hard times — пережить трудные времена; give up on — бросать, сдаваться; put into perspective — помочь взглянуть трезво
    Разбор: Ответ идёт по пунктам карточки и заканчивается выводом. Сильные места: would для привычек в прошлом (he'd sit with me), Present Perfect (has lived through, I've never heard), связки on top of that, yet, whenever.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. What can young people learn from older generations?

      A great deal, I think. Older people have seen fashions and crises come and go, so they tend to have a calmer view of life. They can teach practical skills too, like cooking or repairing things, which many young people have never had to learn.

    2. Are old people respected enough in your country?

      Generally, yes. In my culture the oldest person is served first at the table and their opinion carries a lot of weight in family decisions. That said, in big cities things are changing, and some elderly people do end up feeling rather isolated.

    3. Why do some young people ignore advice from the elderly?

      Partly because the world has changed so quickly that the advice can sound out of date, especially about careers or technology. I also think young people simply want to make their own mistakes. It's often only later that we realise how right our grandparents were.

    2. Describe a person who taught you a new skill when you were a child.NEW
    You should say:
    • who this person was
    • what skill they taught you
    • how they taught you
    • and explain how you felt about learning it
    Part 3:
    • Is it better to learn from a teacher or from a family member?
    • What skills should every child learn before leaving school?
    • Is it harder to learn new skills as an adult?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    The person I'd like to describe is my aunt, who taught me how to ride a bicycle when I was about six. At that time we lived in the same courtyard, and she was a university student with a lot more patience than my parents. I'd been given a second-hand bike for my birthday, but I was terrified of falling off. Her method was quite clever. Instead of holding the saddle the whole time, she took the pedals off and told me to push myself along with my feet, so that I learned to balance first. After a few days she put the pedals back on, and one evening she ran beside me for a while and then quietly let go. I didn't even notice until I heard her cheering behind me. I felt incredibly proud, as if I'd learned to fly. Looking back, I think she taught me more than cycling. She showed me that a frightening task becomes manageable if you break it down into small steps, and I still use that approach when I'm studying.

    Лексика: be terrified of — ужасно бояться; let go — отпустить; manageable — посильный; break it down into steps — разбить на шаги; looking back — оглядываясь назад
    Разбор: Хороший рассказ в прошедших временах: Past Perfect для предыстории (I'd been given), Past Simple для цепочки событий, вывод в настоящем (I still use). Сравнение as if I'd learned to fly добавляет лексику.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. Is it better to learn from a teacher or from a family member?

      It depends on the skill. A family member has more time and knows the child's personality, which helps with things like cycling or cooking. For academic subjects, though, a trained teacher is usually better, because relatives tend to lose patience or explain things in a confusing way.

    2. What skills should every child learn before leaving school?

      I'd say basic cooking, managing money and how to swim. These are things you need for the rest of your life, and schools often overlook them in favour of exams. I'd add learning how to check whether information online is reliable.

    3. Is it harder to learn new skills as an adult?

      In some ways, yes. Adults are busier and more afraid of looking foolish, so they give up sooner. On the other hand, they're better at organising their learning and they usually have a clear reason for doing it, which keeps them motivated.

    3. Describe a person you know who you think is very happy.NEW
    You should say:
    • who this person is
    • how you know them
    • what they do in daily life
    • and explain why you think they are so happy
    Part 3:
    • Does money make people happy?
    • Are people today happier than in the past?
    • Can people learn to be happier?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'm going to talk about a friend of my father's called Rustam, who runs a small bakery in our neighbourhood. I've known him since I was a child, because we buy our bread from him almost every morning. He gets up at four to light the oven, works on his feet for ten hours, and has never, as far as I know, taken a proper holiday. You'd expect him to be exhausted and grumpy, but he's the most cheerful person I've ever met. He knows every customer by name, he's always humming some old song, and he slips an extra pastry into the bag for children. I think he's happy for a few reasons. Firstly, he genuinely loves what he does and takes pride in it. Secondly, he's surrounded by people all day, and he seems to get energy from those little conversations. And finally, he doesn't compare himself with anyone. He once told me that he has enough, and that enough is plenty. I find that attitude rare and rather inspiring.

    Лексика: run a bakery — держать пекарню; grumpy — ворчливый; take pride in — гордиться своим делом; hum — напевать; compare oneself with — сравнивать себя с
    Разбор: Структура «портрет → примеры → причины (firstly, secondly, and finally) → оценка». You'd expect him to… but… — удачный контраст; превосходная степень + Present Perfect (the most cheerful person I've ever met).
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. Does money make people happy?

      Only up to a point. Money certainly removes stress if you can't pay your bills, so being poor makes happiness difficult. But once people have enough to live comfortably, extra income doesn't seem to make much difference compared with health and relationships.

    2. Are people today happier than in the past?

      That's hard to say. We're certainly more comfortable and healthier than our grandparents were. However, people nowadays seem more anxious, perhaps because social media makes us compare our lives with everybody else's all the time.

    3. Can people learn to be happier?

      I believe so, to some extent. Habits like keeping in touch with friends, exercising and being grateful for small things have been shown to lift people's mood. Of course, personality plays a part too, so it comes more naturally to some than to others.

    4. Describe a person you know who is good at making things (by hand or using technology).NEW
    You should say:
    • who this person is
    • what they make
    • how they learned to do it
    • and explain why you think they are good at it
    Part 3:
    • Are handmade products better than factory-made ones?
    • Should schools teach practical skills such as woodwork or sewing?
    • Will traditional crafts disappear in the future?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'd like to tell you about my cousin Dilshod, who is brilliant at making things out of wood. He's a few years older than me and works as an accountant, but carpentry is what he really loves. He makes all sorts of things, from chopping boards and stools to a full-sized bookcase that now stands in my room. What impresses me is that he's completely self-taught. He started about five years ago by watching videos online, bought a few second-hand tools, and turned a corner of his father's garage into a workshop. His first attempts were, frankly, a bit wobbly, but he kept at it. I think he's good at it for two reasons. He's extremely precise, which probably comes from his job, so he measures everything three times before he cuts. And he has real patience. He once spent an entire weekend sanding a single table top until it was perfectly smooth. Watching him work has made me appreciate handmade things, and last year he even taught me how to make a simple shelf.

    Лексика: self-taught — самоучка; wobbly — шаткий; keep at it — не бросать, упорно продолжать; precise — точный; appreciate — ценить
    Разбор: Сильные места: придаточные (which probably comes from his job), from… to…, вставные слова frankly. Ответ закрывается личным следствием — это даёт завершённость.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. Are handmade products better than factory-made ones?

      Often they are, in terms of quality and character, because the maker cares about every detail. But they're also much more expensive and take longer to produce. For everyday items like phones or cars, factory production is clearly more reliable.

    2. Should schools teach practical skills such as woodwork or sewing?

      I think they should. Not everyone is academic, and subjects like woodwork give practical students a chance to shine. Besides, being able to fix a shelf or sew on a button is useful for anyone, whatever career they choose.

    3. Will traditional crafts disappear in the future?

      Some probably will, as the older generation of craftspeople retires. Still, I'm fairly optimistic, because there's growing interest in handmade goods, and the internet lets makers sell directly to customers all over the world.

    5. Describe a person you know who is popular with many people.NEW
    You should say:
    • who this person is
    • how you know them
    • what they are like
    • and explain why so many people like them
    Part 3:
    • What qualities make a person popular?
    • Is being popular important for teenagers?
    • Do popular people always make good leaders?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    The person who comes to mind is a classmate of mine called Kamila. We met in our first year at university, and it seems as though half the campus knows her. She isn't loud or particularly fashionable, which is what you might expect of a popular person. She's simply one of the warmest people I know. She remembers small details about everyone, like the name of your younger brother or the fact that you had a dentist's appointment, and she asks about them later. She's also a fantastic listener. When you talk to her, she puts her phone away and gives you her full attention, which is surprisingly rare these days. Another reason people like her is that she never gossips. You can trust that whatever you tell her will stay with her. And she has a great sense of humour, mostly at her own expense. I think her popularity comes down to one thing: she makes other people feel important. I've actually tried to copy some of her habits, and it has improved my own friendships.

    Лексика: come to mind — приходить на ум; give full attention — уделять всё внимание; gossip — сплетничать; at her own expense — над собой; come down to — сводиться к
    Разбор: Приём «ожидание → опровержение» (She isn't loud… which is what you might expect). Много придаточных: which is surprisingly rare, whatever you tell her. Финал связывает рассказ с говорящим.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. What qualities make a person popular?

      Kindness and a sense of humour, above all. People are drawn to those who make them feel comfortable. Confidence helps too, but only if it doesn't turn into arrogance. Being a good listener is probably the most underrated quality.

    2. Is being popular important for teenagers?

      It feels extremely important at that age, because teenagers are working out who they are and badly want to belong. Looking back, though, most adults realise that having two or three loyal friends mattered far more than being admired by the whole class.

    3. Do popular people always make good leaders?

      Not necessarily. Popular people are good at winning support, which is useful, but a leader sometimes has to make unpopular decisions. Someone who needs to be liked by everyone may avoid doing what is actually right.

    6. Describe a person you know who is well organised.NEW
    You should say:
    • who this person is
    • how you know them
    • what they do to stay organised
    • and explain how you feel about this person
    Part 3:
    • How can parents help children to be organised?
    • Does technology make people more or less organised?
    • Is being organised more important at work or at home?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'd like to describe my older sister, Nilufar, who is easily the most organised person I know. She's a junior doctor, so her schedule is brutal, and yet she never seems to forget anything. Her system is quite simple. Every Sunday evening she sits down with a paper planner and maps out the whole week, including meals and exercise. She colour-codes everything: blue for work, green for family, and so on. She also prepares things the night before. Her clothes are laid out, her bag is packed, and her lunch is in the fridge, so mornings are completely stress-free. At home, everything has its place. If you borrow her scissors, she notices within the hour. To be honest, I used to find it slightly irritating, because I'm the opposite. But during my exams last year I was drowning in deadlines, and she sat down and helped me draw up a revision timetable. It made such a difference that I've kept the habit. So now my feeling is mostly admiration, with just a little envy.

    Лексика: map out the week — расписать неделю; lay out clothes — разложить одежду; be drowning in deadlines — тонуть в дедлайнах; draw up a timetable — составить расписание; envy — зависть
    Разбор: Present Simple для привычек + used to для прошлого отношения (I used to find it irritating) — показывает изменение. Пассив (her clothes are laid out, her bag is packed) расширяет грамматику.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. How can parents help children to be organised?

      Mostly by example and by giving them small responsibilities, like packing their own school bag or tidying their toys at a fixed time. A simple routine works better than constant reminders. Praise helps as well, when the child manages it without being told.

    2. Does technology make people more or less organised?

      Both, really. Calendars and reminder apps mean you never have to miss an appointment. At the same time, constant notifications break your concentration, so plenty of people end up busier but less organised than before.

    3. Is being organised more important at work or at home?

      At work the consequences are more serious, since a missed deadline can affect a whole team. But I'd argue the habit starts at home. Someone whose personal life is chaotic usually finds it hard to be disciplined in the office.

    7. Describe a person you know who did something to improve their health and fitness.NEW
    You should say:
    • who this person is
    • what they did
    • how difficult it was for them
    • and explain what the results were
    Part 3:
    • Why do many people find it hard to keep fit?
    • Should governments do more to promote healthy lifestyles?
    • Are gyms necessary for staying fit?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'm going to talk about my uncle Bakhtiyor, who completely changed his lifestyle about three years ago. He's in his early fifties and works as a taxi driver, so he used to spend twelve hours a day sitting down and living on fried food and sweet tea. Then his doctor warned him that his blood pressure was dangerously high. That gave him a real fright, and he decided to act. He started small. At first he simply parked the car and walked for twenty minutes during his lunch break. Then he gave up sugary drinks, which he says was the hardest part, and began bringing home-cooked meals instead of buying fast food. After a few months he joined a group of men who play football in the park every morning at six. It was tough at the beginning. He told me that in the first week he could barely get out of bed because his legs ached so much. But he stuck with it, and the results have been remarkable. He's lost about fifteen kilos, his blood pressure is normal, and he looks ten years younger.

    Лексика: give someone a fright — сильно напугать; give up — отказаться от; stick with it — не бросить; ache — болеть, ныть; remarkable — поразительный
    Разбор: Чёткая хронология (then, at first, after a few months, at the beginning). Used to для прежних привычек, Present Perfect для результата (he's lost, have been remarkable). Косвенная речь: he told me that…
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. Why do many people find it hard to keep fit?

      Mainly a lack of time and energy. After a long day at work, the sofa is far more tempting than the gym. Results also come slowly, so people lose motivation before they see any change. Having a friend to exercise with makes a big difference.

    2. Should governments do more to promote healthy lifestyles?

      I think so, because poor health costs society a fortune in the end. They could build more cycle lanes and public sports grounds and limit the advertising of junk food. However, they can only encourage people. The final decision is personal.

    3. Are gyms necessary for staying fit?

      Not at all. They're convenient, especially in bad weather, but you can get perfectly fit by walking briskly, running or doing exercises at home. What matters is doing something regularly, and a gym membership doesn't guarantee that.

    8. Describe a person you know who likes learning about history.NEW
    You should say:
    • who this person is
    • how they learn about history
    • what period or topic interests them
    • and explain why they enjoy it
    Part 3:
    • Why should children study history at school?
    • Are museums the best way to learn about the past?
    • Can films teach history accurately?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    The person I have in mind is my former neighbour, Mr Karimov, a retired schoolteacher who is absolutely passionate about history. He must be in his seventies now. He mainly learns by reading. His flat is like a small library, with shelves from floor to ceiling, and he also spends a lot of time in the city archive looking at old maps and newspapers. Recently he's discovered history podcasts, which he listens to while walking. The period he's most interested in is the era of the Silk Road, particularly the history of our own city. He can tell you which caravans stopped here, what they traded and where the old city gates used to stand. I think he enjoys it for a couple of reasons. One is simple curiosity: he says every answer leads to three new questions. The other is that it connects him to the place where he's lived all his life. When I was a teenager he took me on a walk around the old town and brought every street to life. It was far more interesting than any history lesson I'd had.

    Лексика: be passionate about — страстно увлекаться; from floor to ceiling — от пола до потолка; era — эпоха; bring to life — оживить; curiosity — любознательность
    Разбор: Удачная модальность: He must be in his seventies (предположение). Причины поданы связкой One is… The other is…. Сравнение в конце (far more interesting than any lesson I'd had) — Past Perfect.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. Why should children study history at school?

      Because it explains how the present came about and helps them judge what they read in the news. It also teaches skills, such as weighing evidence and spotting bias. Without it, people are easier to mislead.

    2. Are museums the best way to learn about the past?

      They're one good way, since seeing a real object makes the past feel concrete. But a museum can only show a small part of the story. I'd say a combination of museums, books and good teachers works best.

    3. Can films teach history accurately?

      They can give a vivid impression of a period, the clothes and the atmosphere, and they often spark an interest. But film-makers change facts to make a better story, so I wouldn't rely on them. They're a starting point, not a source.

    9. Describe a person you know who enjoys taking a lot of photos.NEW
    You should say:
    • who this person is
    • what they like to photograph
    • what they do with the photos
    • and explain why they enjoy it so much
    Part 3:
    • Why do people take so many photos nowadays?
    • Are printed photos better than digital ones?
    • Do people spend too much time photographing instead of enjoying the moment?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'd like to talk about my friend Aziz, who seems to see the whole world through a camera lens. We've been friends since school, and I can't remember ever seeing him without a camera or at least his phone in his hand. He photographs almost everything, but his favourite subjects are street scenes: old men playing chess in the park, sellers at the market, children chasing pigeons. He prefers taking pictures of people when they aren't posing. As for what he does with the photos, he's quite selective. Out of a hundred shots he might keep five. He edits those and posts them on his page, which now has several thousand followers, and last year a few were shown at a small exhibition at our university. I think he enjoys it so much because it makes him notice things that the rest of us walk past. He once said that photography forces him to slow down and really look. It's also his way of keeping a diary. He can show you a picture from four years ago and tell you exactly what the weather was like that day.

    Лексика: see the world through a lens — смотреть на мир через объектив; pose — позировать; selective — избирательный; shot — снимок; slow down — замедлиться
    Разбор: Present Perfect для длительности (We've been friends since school). As for… — хорошая связка для перехода к пункту карточки. Модальность might keep, придаточные that the rest of us walk past.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. Why do people take so many photos nowadays?

      Simply because it's so easy. Everyone has a good camera in their pocket and storage costs nothing. Photos have also become a form of communication. People send a picture instead of writing a message.

    2. Are printed photos better than digital ones?

      I think printed photos are more special. You put them in an album or on a wall and look at them for years. Digital ones are convenient, but most of them stay on a phone and are never seen again.

    3. Do people spend too much time photographing instead of enjoying the moment?

      Quite often, yes. You see people at concerts watching the whole show through their screens. I think a few photos are fine, but if you're busy recording everything, you can miss the actual experience.

    10. Describe a sportsperson you know about who did very well at an event.NEW
    You should say:
    • who the person is
    • what the event was
    • what they achieved
    • and explain how you felt about their performance
    Part 3:
    • Should top athletes be paid such high salaries?
    • What makes a successful athlete, talent or hard work?
    • Do international sports events bring countries together?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'm going to describe the boxer Bakhodir Jalolov, who is one of the best-known sportsmen in Uzbekistan. I'm not a huge boxing fan, but I remember watching the final of the Olympic Games in Tokyo with my whole family. He's a super-heavyweight, very tall, around two metres, and he was one of the leaders of our team. In that tournament he won every fight convincingly, and in the final he controlled the match from the first round and took the gold medal. What made it special was the context. The Games had been postponed for a year, athletes had trained in very difficult conditions, and there were no spectators in the hall. Even so, he looked completely calm. When the result was announced, everyone in our living room jumped up and my grandmother actually cried. I felt enormously proud. What I admire about him is his discipline and the fact that he stayed modest in the interviews afterwards, thanking his coaches rather than talking about himself. It made a lot of boys in my neighbourhood take up boxing.

    Лексика: convincingly — убедительно; postpone — отложить; spectator — зритель; modest — скромный; take up — начать заниматься
    Разбор: Past Perfect для фона (had been postponed, had trained), Past Simple для событий. Подставь своего спортсмена и проверь факты о нём: экзаменатор оценивает язык, но рассказ должен быть уверенным.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. Should top athletes be paid such high salaries?

      It's a difficult question. Their careers are short and they bring pleasure to millions, so high pay is understandable. But when a footballer earns more in a week than a nurse does in ten years, it does seem out of proportion.

    2. What makes a successful athlete, talent or hard work?

      Both, but I'd put hard work first. Talent gets you noticed, yet there are plenty of gifted people who never reach the top because they lack discipline. The very best combine the two.

    3. Do international sports events bring countries together?

      To some extent. During a big tournament people from different countries share the same excitement, and athletes often show respect to each other. On the other hand, sport can also stir up nationalism, so the effect isn't always positive.

    11. Describe a childhood friend who you remember well.
    You should say:
    • who this friend was
    • how you met
    • what you used to do together
    • and explain why you remember them well
    Part 3:
    • Is it easy to keep childhood friendships as an adult?
    • How do children make friends differently from adults?
    • Has social media changed friendship?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'd like to talk about my childhood friend Sardor. We met when we were five, on the first day of kindergarten, because we were both crying and the teacher sat us together. After that we were inseparable for about ten years. We lived on the same street, so we spent every free hour together. In summer we'd play football until it got dark, and then lie on the roof of his garage looking at the stars. We also built a rather dangerous treehouse, which our parents made us take down. I remember him so well because he was fearless and I was cautious, and somehow we balanced each other. He'd talk me into adventures and I'd talk him out of the really stupid ones. When we were fifteen his family moved to another city, and it felt like losing a brother. We still message each other on birthdays, and when we do meet, it's as if no time has passed. I think the friends you make as a child know a version of you that nobody else ever will.

    Лексика: inseparable — неразлучные; fearless — бесстрашный; cautious — осторожный; talk someone into / out of — уговорить / отговорить; as if no time has passed — будто и не расставались
    Разбор: Would для повторяющихся действий в прошлом (we'd play, he'd talk me into). Пара talk into / talk out of показывает владение фразовыми глаголами. Финальная мысль обобщает рассказ.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. Is it easy to keep childhood friendships as an adult?

      Not really. People move away, start families and develop different interests, so it takes real effort. The friendships that survive are usually the ones where both sides don't mind long gaps between conversations.

    2. How do children make friends differently from adults?

      Children become friends almost instantly, simply because they're playing in the same place. Adults are more careful. They usually need a shared interest or workplace, and it takes much longer to build trust.

    3. Has social media changed friendship?

      It has, in both directions. It's much easier to stay in contact with people far away. But many online friendships are quite shallow. Having five hundred contacts isn't the same as having someone who'll help you move house.

    12. Describe a person you know who did something difficult and was successful.
    You should say:
    • who this person is
    • what they did
    • why it was difficult
    • and explain how you felt about their success
    Part 3:
    • Is failure important for success?
    • Do successful people have a duty to help others?
    • How do people in your country define success?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    The person I'd like to talk about is my mother, who went back to university at the age of forty-three. She had trained as a nurse when she was young, but she had always wanted to qualify as a pharmacist. For years it seemed impossible, with three children and a full-time job. Then one day she simply announced that she had applied for an evening course. It was difficult in almost every way. She'd finish a shift at the hospital, cook dinner, and then study chemistry at the kitchen table until midnight. She hadn't sat an exam for more than twenty years, and she was by far the oldest student in her group. I remember her failing one test in the first term and nearly giving up. But she pulled herself together, found a study partner half her age, and passed everything in the end. Four years later we all went to her graduation. I felt so proud that I could hardly speak. It taught me that it's never too late, and whenever I complain about my own workload, I remember that kitchen table.

    Лексика: qualify as — получить квалификацию; sit an exam — сдавать экзамен; pull oneself together — взять себя в руки; in the end — в конце концов; workload — нагрузка
    Разбор: Past Perfect (had trained, had always wanted, hadn't sat) задаёт предысторию. Конструкция so… that (so proud that I could hardly speak). Герундий после remember (remember her failing).
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. Is failure important for success?

      Very much so. You learn far more from what goes wrong than from what goes smoothly. Most successful people have failed several times first. What matters is how quickly you recover and whether you change your approach.

    2. Do successful people have a duty to help others?

      I'd say they have a moral duty, though not a legal one. Nobody succeeds entirely alone. They've had teachers, family and some luck, so giving something back seems fair, whether through money, advice or creating jobs.

    3. How do people in your country define success?

      Traditionally, by a stable job, a house and a well-raised family. Younger people are starting to define it differently, though, putting more weight on doing work they enjoy and having time for themselves.

    13. Describe a person you know about who has a successful business.
    You should say:
    • who this person is
    • what the business is
    • how they built it
    • and explain why you think it is successful
    Part 3:
    • Is it better to work for yourself or for a company?
    • What difficulties do small businesses face?
    • Should schools teach children about business?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'm going to talk about a woman called Madina, who owns a chain of small coffee shops in my city. I don't know her personally, but I've read interviews with her, and one of my friends works for her. About eight years ago she was working in a bank and was, in her own words, bored to tears. She noticed that there was nowhere in her district to get a decent coffee, so she rented a tiny space, bought a second-hand machine and opened a kiosk. She did everything herself at first, from serving customers to mopping the floor. Now she has seven branches and employs around sixty people. I think her business is successful for three reasons. First, the quality is consistent: the coffee tastes the same in every branch. Second, she treats her staff well, pays them above the average and trains them properly, so they stay. And third, she listens. My friend says she still spends one day a week behind the counter, talking to customers. What I admire is that she took a risk when she had a safe job.

    Лексика: bored to tears — смертельно скучно; branch — филиал; consistent — стабильный; treat staff well — хорошо относиться к сотрудникам; take a risk — рискнуть
    Разбор: Чёткая организация причин (First… Second… And third…). Past Continuous для фона (she was working), in her own words — способ передать чужую речь. Двоеточие-пояснение передаётся паузой.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. Is it better to work for yourself or for a company?

      Each has its advantages. Being your own boss gives you freedom and the rewards are all yours, but so are the risks and the long hours. A company offers a steady salary and less stress. Personally, I'd like some experience as an employee first.

    2. What difficulties do small businesses face?

      The biggest is usually money, especially in the first year, when costs are high and customers are few. They also struggle to compete with big chains on price, and the paperwork and taxes can be overwhelming for one person.

    3. Should schools teach children about business?

      I think a basic introduction would be valuable. Even students who never start a company would benefit from understanding budgets, taxes and how to sell an idea. It should be practical, though, such as running a small project, not just theory.

    14. Describe a person you know who is good at learning languages.
    You should say:
    • who this person is
    • which languages they know
    • how they learn them
    • and explain why you think they are good at it
    Part 3:
    • Why do some people learn languages faster than others?
    • Will translation apps make language learning unnecessary?
    • What is the best age to start a foreign language?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'd like to describe my university classmate Jasur, who has a real gift for languages. He speaks five: Uzbek and Russian from childhood, then English, Turkish and Korean, which he's still improving. What makes him interesting is his method. He doesn't spend much time on textbooks. Instead, he throws himself into the language from the first day. When he started Korean, he changed the language on his phone, watched dramas with Korean subtitles, and found a language partner online within a week. He keeps a small notebook of phrases he actually hears people say, and he repeats them out loud while walking. I think he's good at it for a few reasons. He has an excellent ear, so his pronunciation is very natural. But more importantly, he isn't afraid of sounding silly. Most of us stay silent until we're sure a sentence is correct, whereas he just talks, makes mistakes and laughs about them. He's also very consistent. He does half an hour every day without fail. Watching him has changed the way I study English.

    Лексика: have a gift for — иметь талант к; throw oneself into — с головой погрузиться; have a good ear — иметь хороший слух; out loud — вслух; without fail — непременно
    Разбор: Контраст whereas (Most of us stay silent… whereas he just talks). Present Perfect в конце (has changed the way I study). Перечисление причин с But more importantly — показывает ранжирование идей.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. Why do some people learn languages faster than others?

      Partly natural ability, such as a good memory and a good ear. But I think attitude matters more. People who aren't afraid of mistakes practise far more, and those with a strong reason to learn, like moving abroad, progress fastest.

    2. Will translation apps make language learning unnecessary?

      They'll certainly reduce the need for tourists or for simple business messages. But a language is also a way of understanding a culture and building relationships. I can't imagine making a close friend through an app.

    3. What is the best age to start a foreign language?

      The earlier the better for pronunciation, I'd say around five or six. Young children pick up sounds effortlessly. That said, older learners have better study skills, so it's never too late to start.

    15. Describe a person you know who likes growing plants at home or in a garden.
    You should say:
    • who this person is
    • what they grow
    • how much time they spend on it
    • and explain why they like it
    Part 3:
    • Why is gardening popular among older people?
    • Should cities have more community gardens?
    • Is it important for children to learn how food is grown?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    The person I want to talk about is my grandmother, who has what people call green fingers. She lives in a house with a courtyard, and every corner of it is full of plants. She grows a mixture of things. There are roses and basil along the wall, a grapevine that covers the whole yard like a roof, and a vegetable patch with tomatoes, cucumbers and herbs. On the windowsills she keeps pots of geraniums. She spends a couple of hours out there every day, early in the morning before it gets hot and again in the evening. In summer it's practically a full-time job, with all the watering. I think she loves it for several reasons. She grew up in a village, so working with the soil reminds her of her childhood. It also keeps her active. She says the garden is her gym. And she gets real joy from sharing. Nobody leaves her house without a bag of tomatoes or a bunch of herbs. For me, the smell of basil will always mean her courtyard.

    Лексика: have green fingers — уметь выращивать растения; grapevine — виноградная лоза; vegetable patch — грядка; windowsill — подоконник; a bunch of herbs — пучок зелени
    Разбор: There is/are для описания, Present Simple для привычек, идиома green fingers. Финальная сенсорная деталь (the smell of basil) делает ответ запоминающимся.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. Why is gardening popular among older people?

      I think it suits their pace of life. It's gentle exercise, it gets them outdoors and it gives them something to look after once their children have left home. Seeing things grow is also very satisfying.

    2. Should cities have more community gardens?

      Definitely. Not everyone has a garden, and a shared plot lets people in flats grow their own food. It also brings neighbours together who might otherwise never speak, and it makes the area greener.

    3. Is it important for children to learn how food is grown?

      Yes, I think it is. Many city children believe vegetables come from the supermarket. If they grow something themselves, they understand the effort involved and are more willing to eat healthy food and less likely to waste it.

    16. Describe someone you know who has always wanted to work in medicine (doctor, nurse or vet).
    You should say:
    • who this person is
    • what job they want
    • what they are doing to achieve it
    • and explain why they want this career
    Part 3:
    • Why is medicine a respected profession?
    • Should doctors be paid more than other professionals?
    • Will AI replace doctors in the future?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'd like to talk about my school friend Malika, who has wanted to be a doctor for as long as I've known her. When we were about eight, she used to bandage her dolls and take the temperature of everyone in the class. The job she's aiming for is paediatrician, a children's doctor. To get there, she's worked incredibly hard. She studied biology and chemistry for several hours a day throughout secondary school, and she got into medical school on her second attempt, after missing by a few points the first time. She's now in her third year. Besides her lectures, she volunteers at a children's hospital at weekends, mostly reading to patients and helping the nurses. As for why she wants this career, there's a personal reason. Her younger brother was seriously ill as a baby, and she remembers how kind the doctors were to her frightened parents. She says she wants to be that person for another family. Knowing how determined she is, I have no doubt she'll make it.

    Лексика: for as long as I've known her — сколько я её знаю; aim for — стремиться к; get into medical school — поступить в медицинский; on her second attempt — со второй попытки; determined — целеустремлённый
    Разбор: Present Perfect для длительного желания (has wanted… for as long as I've known her), used to для детства. As for why… — переход к последнему пункту. Причастный оборот в конце (Knowing how determined she is).
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. Why is medicine a respected profession?

      Because doctors literally hold people's lives in their hands, and the training is long and demanding. People trust them with their most private problems. That combination of knowledge and responsibility earns a great deal of respect.

    2. Should doctors be paid more than other professionals?

      In many countries they're underpaid for the hours they work and the pressure they're under, so yes, I think they deserve more. If salaries are too low, talented doctors move abroad, and the whole health system suffers.

    3. Will AI replace doctors in the future?

      I doubt it will replace them entirely. Software is already very good at reading scans and spotting patterns, so it'll take over some tasks. But patients need someone to explain, reassure and take responsibility, and that requires a human being.

    Places

    17. Describe a public building you enjoy spending time in (e.g. a library or sports centre).NEW
    You should say:
    • what the building is
    • where it is
    • what you do there
    • and explain why you enjoy spending time there
    Part 3:
    • Who should pay for public buildings such as libraries?
    • Are libraries still needed in the digital age?
    • How important is the design of public buildings?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'd like to talk about the central library in my city, which is the public building I spend the most time in. It's in the city centre, a short walk from the main square. It's a large modern building with a glass front, and the reading rooms on the upper floors look out over a park. I go there three or four times a week, mainly to study. I find it almost impossible to concentrate at home, where there's always a television on or someone calling me to help in the kitchen. At the library, everybody around you is working, and that atmosphere is contagious. I usually take a desk by the window on the third floor. Apart from studying, I sometimes go to the free lectures they hold on Saturday afternoons, and there's a small café on the ground floor where I meet friends. What I enjoy most is the quiet. It's one of the very few places in the city where nobody expects you to buy anything or to hurry. You can sit for six hours with one book, and that feels like a luxury.

    Лексика: look out over — выходить окнами на; contagious — заразительный; apart from — помимо; on the ground floor — на первом этаже; feel like a luxury — казаться роскошью
    Разбор: Описание места в Present Simple + придаточные места и причины (where there's always…, where nobody expects you to…). Суперлатив the public building I spend the most time in сразу отвечает на вопрос карточки.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. Who should pay for public buildings such as libraries?

      I think the government should, through taxes, because libraries benefit everyone, including people who could never afford to buy books or pay for internet access. If they depended on entrance fees, the people who need them most would be shut out.

    2. Are libraries still needed in the digital age?

      Yes, though their role has changed. Fewer people come only to borrow books. They've become places to study, use computers and attend events. For students and elderly people especially, they're still extremely valuable.

    3. How important is the design of public buildings?

      Very important. A well-designed building with natural light and comfortable seats makes people want to come in and stay. A dark, unfriendly one puts them off, however good the services inside are.

    18. Describe a place where you enjoy spending time in nature.NEW
    You should say:
    • where the place is
    • how often you go there
    • what you do there
    • and explain why you enjoy it
    Part 3:
    • Why do people in cities need access to nature?
    • Are young people losing contact with nature?
    • Should governments protect more land as national parks?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    The place I'd like to describe is a mountain area called Chimgan, about an hour and a half's drive from Tashkent. I go there three or four times a year, usually with friends from university, and more often in spring and autumn than in the heat of summer. It's a wide valley surrounded by peaks that keep their snow until June, with a river running through it and slopes covered in wild flowers in May. What we do there is quite simple. We leave early, hike for three or four hours along a trail that follows the river, and then have a picnic somewhere with a view. Sometimes we stay overnight in a guesthouse and get up to watch the sunrise. I enjoy it for a few reasons. The air is so clean that you can actually feel the difference in your lungs after the city. There's no phone signal on most of the trail, which forces everyone to talk to each other. And physically, I come back tired but mentally completely refreshed. For me it works better than any holiday.
