    Лексика: peak — вершина; hike — идти в поход; trail — тропа; stay overnight — остаться на ночь; refreshed — отдохнувший
    Разбор: So… that (so clean that you can feel the difference), which-придаточное с оценкой (which forces everyone to talk). Три причины с параллельной структурой. Подставь своё место.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. Why do people in cities need access to nature?

      Because city life is noisy, crowded and stressful, and green spaces give the mind a rest. Research suggests that even a short walk in a park lowers stress. Without that, people become more irritable and less healthy.

    2. Are young people losing contact with nature?

      I'm afraid many are. They spend most of their free time indoors on screens, and some can't name the common trees or birds in their own area. It's a pity, because people protect only what they know and care about.

    3. Should governments protect more land as national parks?

      Yes, I think they should. Once land has been built on, the wildlife doesn't come back. National parks protect species and also give future generations somewhere to experience real wilderness. Tourism there has to be managed carefully, though.

    19. Describe a time when you went to a crowded place.NEW
    You should say:
    • where the place was
    • when you went there
    • why it was so crowded
    • and explain how you felt
    Part 3:
    • Why do some people enjoy crowds while others avoid them?
    • How can cities manage large crowds safely?
    • Are crowded cities good places to live?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'd like to talk about the time I went to the main bazaar in my city on the day before Navruz, our spring holiday. It was last March, and my mother had asked me to help her carry the shopping. The reason it was so crowded is that everybody buys food for the holiday at the same time, and on top of that the weather was beautiful, so half the city seemed to be there. I've never seen anything like it. The lanes between the stalls were so packed that you couldn't choose your own direction. You just moved with the flow of people. Sellers were shouting prices, porters were pushing carts and calling out to clear the way, and the smell of fresh bread and herbs was everywhere. At first I found it overwhelming, and I was worried about losing my mother. At one point I actually did lose her for ten minutes. But after a while I began to enjoy the energy of it. Everyone was in a good mood, strangers were joking with each other, and it really felt like a celebration.

    Лексика: packed — битком набитый; move with the flow — двигаться с потоком; overwhelming — ошеломляющий; clear the way — освободить дорогу; in a good mood — в хорошем настроении
    Разбор: Past Continuous для атмосферы (sellers were shouting, porters were pushing) на фоне Past Simple. Эмфаза I actually did lose her. Развитие чувств at first… but after a while… отвечает на пункт how you felt.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. Why do some people enjoy crowds while others avoid them?

      I think it's partly personality. Outgoing people get energy from being among others, so a festival or a stadium excites them. Quieter people find the noise and lack of space exhausting. Past experience matters as well.

    2. How can cities manage large crowds safely?

      Good planning is essential: enough exits, clear signs, and staff trained to direct people. Limiting numbers through advance tickets helps too. Many cities now use cameras to spot dangerous build-ups before they become serious.

    3. Are crowded cities good places to live?

      They have advantages, such as jobs, entertainment and services close at hand. But overcrowding pushes up housing costs and makes daily travel stressful. Whether it's a good place to live depends on how well the city is run.

    20. Describe a time you went to a place that was very noisy.NEW
    You should say:
    • where the place was
    • why you were there
    • what made it noisy
    • and explain how the noise affected you
    Part 3:
    • Is noise a serious problem in cities?
    • Should there be laws against noise at night?
    • Why do some people need silence to work?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'm going to describe my cousin's wedding, which was probably the noisiest place I've ever been. It took place last summer in a large banquet hall, and I was there as a family member, so leaving early wasn't an option. Weddings in my country tend to be huge. There were about four hundred guests. The main source of the noise was the music. A live band was playing traditional songs through enormous speakers, and I happened to be sitting at a table right next to them. On top of that, there were drums and long trumpets when the bride and groom came in, and hundreds of people talking over the music. The effect on me was mixed. For the first hour it was exciting, and I even danced, which I rarely do. But after three hours my ears were ringing and I'd almost lost my voice from shouting to the person beside me. I ended up stepping outside every half hour just to hear myself think. I had a slight headache the next day, but I wouldn't have missed it.

    Лексика: banquet hall — банкетный зал; bride and groom — жених и невеста; my ears were ringing — в ушах звенело; hear myself think — собраться с мыслями; I wouldn't have missed it — я бы ни за что это не пропустил
    Разбор: I happened to be sitting — естественная конструкция; Past Perfect (I'd almost lost my voice); третий тип условного в конце (I wouldn't have missed it). Ответ закрывает пункт how the noise affected you.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. Is noise a serious problem in cities?

      Yes, I'd say it is. Traffic, construction and loud music from cafés go on from early morning until late at night. People get used to it, but studies link constant noise to poor sleep and stress.

    2. Should there be laws against noise at night?

      I think so, within reason. Most people need to sleep between about eleven and seven, and one inconsiderate neighbour can ruin the night for a whole building. The rules should allow exceptions for special occasions, though.

    3. Why do some people need silence to work?

      Because tasks like reading or writing use the same part of the brain that processes speech and sound. Some people can filter out background noise, but for others every conversation nearby is a distraction.

    21. Describe a short journey you often make that you really do not like.NEW
    You should say:
    • where you go
    • how often you make the journey
    • how you travel
    • and explain why you dislike it
    Part 3:
    • How could public transport in your city be improved?
    • Will remote work reduce commuting in the future?
    • Why do people still prefer cars to public transport?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    The journey I'd like to describe is my daily trip from home to university by minibus. It's only about six kilometres, and I make it twice a day, five days a week. On a quiet Sunday it would take fifteen minutes. In the morning rush hour it takes at least forty-five. There are several things I dislike about it. The first is the overcrowding. The minibuses are designed for about fifteen people, and somehow thirty squeeze in, so I usually stand bent over with someone's bag in my face. The second is the traffic. There's one junction near a bridge where we can sit without moving for ten minutes. And the third is the unpredictability. I never know whether I'll arrive early or miss the start of my first lecture. In summer it's even worse because there's no air conditioning. I've tried to make it bearable by listening to English podcasts, and I've calculated that I get through about five hours a week that way. Once the new metro line opens next year, I'll be able to do the whole trip in twenty minutes, and I honestly can't wait.

    Лексика: rush hour — час пик; squeeze in — втиснуться; junction — перекрёсток; bearable — терпимый; I can't wait — жду не дождусь
    Разбор: Условное II (On a quiet Sunday it would take…), придаточное времени с будущим (Once the new line opens, I'll be able to). Перечисление The first… The second… And the third… делает ответ очень связным.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. How could public transport in your city be improved?

      It needs more buses at peak times and dedicated bus lanes, so that buses aren't stuck in the same traffic as cars. A single ticket for all types of transport and reliable timetables shown on an app would also help.

    2. Will remote work reduce commuting in the future?

      To a degree. People who can work from home two or three days a week already travel far less. But many jobs, in hospitals, shops and factories, can't be done remotely, so commuting won't disappear.

    3. Why do people still prefer cars to public transport?

      Mainly for comfort and freedom. A car takes you from door to door whenever you like, and you're guaranteed a seat. Until public transport is as quick and reliable, many drivers won't give that up.

    22. Describe a place you went to on holiday that you would recommend.
    You should say:
    • where it is
    • when you went there
    • what you did there
    • and explain why you would recommend it
    Part 3:
    • Is tourism always good for local people?
    • Do people prefer holidays abroad or in their own country?
    • How has travel changed in recent years?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'd like to recommend Bukhara, an ancient city in my country that I visited with my family two years ago during the spring break. We spent four days there. What makes it special is that the old town is not a museum but a living place. People still live in the narrow lanes, and craftsmen work in the same domed markets where merchants traded centuries ago. We did a lot of walking. We climbed up to the old fortress, visited a tower that's nearly nine hundred years old, and spent hours in workshops watching people make knives, carpets and embroidery. In the evenings we sat by a pool in the main square, drinking tea under mulberry trees. I'd recommend it for three reasons. It's compact, so you can see everything on foot. It's far less crowded than more famous destinations, and the people are incredibly hospitable. A family we'd only just met invited us in for dinner. And finally, the food is wonderful. If you go, try to visit in April or October, because the summer is extremely hot.

    Лексика: domed — с куполом; embroidery — вышивка; compact — компактный; hospitable — гостеприимный; on foot — пешком
    Разбор: Not… but… (not a museum but a living place); Past Perfect (a family we'd only just met); совет в конце в форме условного (If you go, try to…). Подставь своё место — структура подойдёт любому.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. Is tourism always good for local people?

      Not always. It creates jobs and brings in money, which is clearly positive. But it can also push up prices, crowd the streets and turn local culture into a show. The benefits need to reach ordinary residents, not just big companies.

    2. Do people prefer holidays abroad or in their own country?

      It varies. Travelling abroad has become a kind of status symbol, so many people dream of it. But domestic holidays are cheaper and simpler, and since the pandemic more people have discovered what their own country has to offer.

    3. How has travel changed in recent years?

      It's become far cheaper and easier to organise. You can book flights and rooms on your phone in minutes and read reviews from other travellers. The downside is that popular places are now much more crowded.

    23. Describe a place you went to where you remember feeling bored.
    You should say:
    • where it was
    • why you went there
    • what you did there
    • and explain why you felt bored
    Part 3:
    • Why do people get bored more easily nowadays?
    • Is boredom good for creativity?
    • How can teachers make lessons less boring?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'm going to tell you about a visit to a government office last year, which was honestly the most boring three hours of my life. I'd gone there to renew my passport. I arrived at nine, took a number from the machine, and discovered that there were sixty people ahead of me. There was nothing to do but wait. The room had rows of plastic chairs, bright white lights, and a screen showing the numbers, which changed about once every five minutes. To make things worse, my phone battery died after half an hour, and I hadn't brought a book. I ended up reading every notice on the wall, some of them twice, and counting the tiles on the floor. I think I felt so bored because I had no control over the situation and nothing to occupy my mind. Time seemed to slow right down. The only interesting moment was when an elderly man started telling me about his grandchildren. Since then I've learned my lesson. I never go anywhere official without a charged phone and something to read.

    Лексика: renew a passport — продлить паспорт; to make things worse — что ещё хуже; occupy my mind — занять голову; time slowed down — время тянулось; learn my lesson — усвоить урок
    Разбор: Past Perfect (I'd gone, I hadn't brought) + Past Simple; there was nothing to do but wait — естественная конструкция; результат в Present Perfect (I've learned my lesson).
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. Why do people get bored more easily nowadays?

      I think it's because we're used to constant entertainment. With a phone in our pocket, we never have to sit with our own thoughts, so even two minutes without stimulation feels uncomfortable.

    2. Is boredom good for creativity?

      I believe it can be. When the mind has nothing to do, it starts to wander, and that's often when new ideas appear. Many writers say their best ideas come on walks or in the shower.

    3. How can teachers make lessons less boring?

      By involving students more. Lessons with discussion, group tasks or a practical element are far more engaging than listening for an hour. Linking the topic to real life helps too, as does a bit of humour.

    24. Describe a person's home you visited that you liked but would not want to live in.
    You should say:
    • whose home it was
    • what it looked like
    • what you liked about it
    • and explain why you would not want to live there
    Part 3:
    • Do people prefer houses or apartments in your country?
    • How will homes change in the future?
    • Is it better to rent or to buy a home?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'd like to describe the home of a friend of my father's, which we visited last autumn. He's an architect, and he's built himself a house in the hills about forty kilometres outside the city. It's a very striking building: almost entirely glass and concrete, on one level, with a flat roof and a living room that seems to hang over the valley. Inside, everything is white and extremely minimal. There's hardly any furniture, no curtains, and not a single object out of place. What I liked was the light and the view. Sitting in that living room at sunset, with the whole valley turning orange below, was unforgettable. I also admired how carefully every detail had been thought through. But I couldn't live there, for two reasons. Firstly, it's very isolated. The nearest shop is a twenty-minute drive away, and I'd miss having people around. Secondly, it felt more like a gallery than a home. I'm someone who leaves books and cups everywhere, and I'd be afraid to touch anything. It's a wonderful place to visit, but I prefer somewhere a bit more lived-in.

    Лексика: striking — эффектный; minimal — минималистичный; out of place — не на месте; think through — продумать; lived-in — обжитой
    Разбор: Герундий как подлежащее (Sitting in that living room… was unforgettable), пассив в Past Perfect (had been thought through), условное II (I'd miss, I'd be afraid). Контраст liked / but couldn't live закрывает оба пункта карточки.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. Do people prefer houses or apartments in your country?

      In cities most people live in apartments, simply because land is expensive. But I think the ideal for many families is still a house with a yard, where several generations can live together and there's room for guests.

    2. How will homes change in the future?

      I expect they'll be smaller, smarter and more energy-efficient, with solar panels and systems that control heating automatically. As more people work remotely, a proper home office will probably become standard too.

    3. Is it better to rent or to buy a home?

      Buying gives you security and something to pass on, and you're not at the mercy of a landlord. Renting offers flexibility, which suits young people who may change jobs or cities. It really depends on your stage of life.

    25. Describe a tall building that you like or dislike.
    You should say:
    • where it is
    • what it looks like
    • what it is used for
    • and explain why you like or dislike it
    Part 3:
    • Why do cities build skyscrapers?
    • Would you like to live in a high-rise building?
    • Should old buildings be replaced by modern ones?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'm going to talk about the Tashkent television tower, which is the tallest structure in my country and a building I've always liked. It stands in the northern part of the city, near a large park, and you can see it from almost anywhere. It's about three hundred and seventy-five metres high and was completed in the nineteen eighties. In terms of appearance, it's a slim concrete shaft supported by three sloping legs, which makes it look a little like a rocket about to take off. At night it's lit up in different colours. Its main purpose is to broadcast television and radio signals, but there's also an observation deck and a revolving restaurant about a hundred metres up. I like it for a mixture of reasons. As a child I thought it was the most exciting thing in the city, and my parents took me up there for my tenth birthday. I remember pressing my nose against the glass and trying to find our house. Even now, when I come back from a trip and see the tower on the horizon, I know I'm home.

    Лексика: slim — стройный, тонкий; shaft — ствол (сооружения); take off — взлетать; observation deck — смотровая площадка; revolving — вращающийся
    Разбор: In terms of appearance… — хорошая связка для описания. Пассив (was completed, is lit up, supported by). Личное воспоминание в конце отвечает на why you like it. Проверь цифры для своего здания.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. Why do cities build skyscrapers?

      Mainly because land in city centres is scarce and expensive, so building upwards is the only way to fit in more offices and homes. There's also an element of prestige. A dramatic skyline shows that a city is wealthy and modern.

    2. Would you like to live in a high-rise building?

      I'd enjoy the view, but I'm not sure about the rest. I'd worry about lifts breaking down and about being so far from the street. I think I'd feel cut off from the neighbourhood.

    3. Should old buildings be replaced by modern ones?

      Only when they're beyond repair or have no historical value. Old buildings give a city its identity. Wherever possible I'd prefer to see them restored and adapted to new uses instead of being knocked down.

    Events and experiences

    26. Describe a time when you watched a film that you didn't like.NEW
    You should say:
    • what the film was
    • when and where you watched it
    • what it was about
    • and explain why you didn't like it
    Part 3:
    • Why do people have such different tastes in films?
    • Are cinemas still popular in your country?
    • Do film reviews influence what people watch?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'd like to talk about a film I watched a few months ago and really didn't enjoy. It was a big-budget science-fiction film, the third or fourth part of a series, and I saw it at the cinema with two friends on its opening weekend. The story was about a team of soldiers trying to stop an alien invasion, although to be honest I'd struggle to tell you more than that, because the plot made very little sense. There were several reasons I disliked it. To begin with, it was far too long, nearly three hours, and at least an hour of that was explosions. The characters were completely flat. I didn't care whether any of them survived. The dialogue was full of clichés, and you could predict every twist ten minutes before it happened. What annoyed me most was that the trailer had been excellent, so my expectations were high. About halfway through I caught myself checking the time. The only good thing was the soundtrack. Since then I've learned to read a few reviews before I buy a ticket.

    Лексика: big-budget — высокобюджетный; make sense — иметь смысл; flat characters — плоские персонажи; twist — поворот сюжета; halfway through — на середине
    Разбор: Условное II (I'd struggle to tell you), Past Perfect (the trailer had been excellent), эмфаза What annoyed me most was that…. Связки to begin with, since then.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. Why do people have such different tastes in films?

      Because taste depends on personality, age and experience. Someone who has had a stressful week may want a light comedy, while another person enjoys being frightened. What we watched as children also shapes what we like.

    2. Are cinemas still popular in your country?

      They are, although less than before streaming became common. People still go for big releases and as a social occasion, but for ordinary films many prefer to wait and watch at home.

    3. Do film reviews influence what people watch?

      To some extent. A very low rating can put people off, and a lot of good reviews create excitement. In the end, though, I think most people rely on recommendations from friends whose taste they trust.

    27. Describe a party you went to where you celebrated a special event.NEW
    You should say:
    • what the event was
    • who was there
    • what you did
    • and explain why it was special
    Part 3:
    • Why are celebrations important for families?
    • Do people spend too much money on parties?
    • How have celebrations changed in your country?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'd like to describe the party we held for my grandparents' golden wedding anniversary, fifty years of marriage, which took place last October. It was held at my uncle's house, in the courtyard, and there were around sixty guests: all their children and grandchildren, a few old friends, and neighbours who had known them for decades. We'd been planning it secretly for a month. On the day, my grandparents thought they were coming for an ordinary family dinner, so they were genuinely astonished when they walked in. There was a long table covered with food, and my cousins and I had made a slideshow of old photographs, some of which they hadn't seen for forty years. Later there was music, and my grandfather, who is over eighty, danced with my grandmother while everybody clapped. What made it special was seeing how moved they were. My grandfather gave a short speech and said that the best thing he'd ever built was this family. I don't think there was a dry eye in the courtyard. It reminded me how lucky we are to still have them.

    Лексика: golden wedding anniversary — золотая свадьба; astonished — поражённый; slideshow — слайд-шоу; moved — растроганный; not a dry eye — никто не сдержал слёз
    Разбор: Past Perfect Continuous (We'd been planning it), Past Perfect (hadn't seen, he'd ever built), косвенная речь (said that the best thing…). Идиома not a dry eye.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. Why are celebrations important for families?

      Because they bring together relatives who may hardly see each other otherwise, and they mark the important stages of life. Shared memories of those days hold a family together.

    2. Do people spend too much money on parties?

      Some certainly do. Weddings in particular can leave families in debt for years, mainly because of social pressure. I think a smaller event with the people who really matter is often more enjoyable.

    3. How have celebrations changed in your country?

      They've become bigger and more commercial. People now hire halls, photographers and decorators for occasions that used to be celebrated quietly at home. At the same time, some younger couples are choosing simpler ceremonies.

    28. Describe an enjoyable evening that you spent with friends.NEW
    You should say:
    • when it was
    • who you were with
    • what you did
    • and explain why you enjoyed it
    Part 3:
    • How do young people usually spend evenings in your country?
    • Is it better to go out or to stay at home with friends?
    • Do adults have enough time for friends?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'm going to talk about an evening I spent with three old school friends last summer, just before one of them left to study abroad. It was a warm Saturday in August. We hadn't planned anything special. We simply met at a tea house in the old part of the city, the kind of place where you sit on raised wooden platforms with cushions, and ordered far too much food. We must have stayed for five hours. We talked about everything: embarrassing stories from school, our plans, our worries about the future. At one point somebody found an old class photo on their phone, and we laughed until our stomachs hurt. Afterwards we walked along the canal, and one of us had brought a guitar, so we sat on the steps and sang rather badly. I enjoyed it for a few reasons. There was no programme and no pressure, just good company. Nobody was looking at a phone. And I think we all knew it might be the last time the four of us would be together for a long while, which made every moment feel more precious.

    Лексика: embarrassing — неловкий; laugh until our stomachs hurt — смеяться до боли в животе; good company — хорошая компания; precious — драгоценный; for a long while — надолго
    Разбор: We must have stayed (предположение о прошлом), Past Perfect (hadn't planned, had brought), might be/would be — будущее в прошедшем. Причины с параллельными короткими предложениями.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. How do young people usually spend evenings in your country?

      Many go to cafés or walk in parks and along the main streets once it's cooler. Others play football or stay at home gaming or watching series. In summer the whole city seems to come alive after sunset.

    2. Is it better to go out or to stay at home with friends?

      Both have their place. Going out gives you a change of scene. But staying in is cheaper and more relaxed. You can cook together and talk without shouting over music. I probably prefer the second.

    3. Do adults have enough time for friends?

      Usually not. Between work, commuting and family, there's very little left over. Friendships at that age take planning, and many people only realise how much they miss their friends when months have gone by.

    29. Describe a time when you had to listen to someone talking, but you weren't very interested.NEW
    You should say:
    • who was talking
    • what they were talking about
    • where you were
    • and explain why you were not interested
    Part 3:
    • What makes a good speaker?
    • Why do people find it hard to concentrate for long?
    • Is it rude to use a phone while someone is talking?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'd like to describe a presentation I had to sit through at a careers day at my university last spring. The speaker was a manager from an insurance company, and the event took place in a large lecture hall after a full day of classes. Attendance was compulsory, so about two hundred of us were there. He was talking about the history and structure of his company: when it was founded, how many branches it has, and what each department does. I wasn't interested for several reasons. Firstly, I have no plans to work in insurance. Secondly, the delivery was very flat. He read every slide word for word in the same tone, and the slides were crammed with small text. And thirdly, it went on for an hour and a half, far longer than announced. I tried to look attentive, but my mind kept drifting to an essay I had to finish. I noticed that half the room was secretly on their phones. The irony is that in the last five minutes he told a funny story about his first interview, and suddenly everybody was listening. It taught me a lot about how not to give a presentation.

    Лексика: sit through — высидеть; compulsory — обязательный; word for word — слово в слово; crammed with — забитый; my mind kept drifting — мысли постоянно уплывали
    Разбор: Keep + -ing (kept drifting), связки Firstly… Secondly… And thirdly…, far longer than announced. The irony is that… — приём для живой концовки.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. What makes a good speaker?

      Enthusiasm, first of all. If the speaker is clearly interested, the audience usually is too. A clear structure, stories and examples, eye contact and a bit of humour all help. And knowing when to stop.

    2. Why do people find it hard to concentrate for long?

      Partly because phones and short videos have trained us to expect something new every few seconds. A long talk without interaction feels slow by comparison. Tiredness and stress also reduce attention.

    3. Is it rude to use a phone while someone is talking?

      In most situations, yes. It tells the speaker that they're less important than a screen. There are exceptions, like taking notes or an urgent call, but then it's polite to explain.

    30. Describe a time when you helped someone with a problem.NEW
    You should say:
    • who you helped
    • what the problem was
    • how you helped
    • and explain how you felt afterwards
    Part 3:
    • Are people less willing to help strangers than in the past?
    • Should children be taught to help others?
    • Why do some people find it hard to ask for help?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'd like to talk about the time I helped an elderly neighbour, Mrs Rahimova, who lives alone on the floor below us. It happened last winter. The problem was that her pension had started being paid onto a bank card, and she had no idea how to use it. She'd been keeping the card in a drawer for two months and borrowing money from relatives, because she was afraid of the cash machine and too embarrassed to ask at the bank. She mentioned it to my mother, and I offered to help. I went with her to the nearest machine and showed her the steps slowly. Then I wrote them out in large letters on a card she could keep in her purse: insert the card, enter the code, choose the amount. We practised three times, and the third time she did it all by herself. I also explained that she should never tell anyone her code. Afterwards I felt really good. It had taken me half an hour, but for her it meant independence. She brought us homemade jam the next day, and now she pays her own bills.

    Лексика: pension — пенсия; cash machine — банкомат; embarrassed — смущённый; by herself — самостоятельно; independence — независимость
    Разбор: Past Perfect и Past Perfect Continuous (had started being paid, she'd been keeping) для предыстории; двоеточие с перечислением шагов; контраст half an hour for me / independence for her.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. Are people less willing to help strangers than in the past?

      In big cities, perhaps. People are in a hurry and more cautious about approaching someone they don't know. But when there's a real emergency, like an accident, most people still stop to help.

    2. Should children be taught to help others?

      Absolutely, and from an early age. Small things, like sharing or carrying a bag for a grandparent, build the habit. Children mostly learn it by watching how their parents behave.

    3. Why do some people find it hard to ask for help?

      Often it's pride. They don't want to look weak or be a burden. Some are afraid of being refused. In my experience, people are usually glad to be asked, because helping makes them feel useful.

    31. Describe an occasion when you received very good service from a company or shop.NEW
    You should say:
    • what the company or shop was
    • what you needed
    • what the staff did
    • and explain why you thought the service was good
    Part 3:
    • What is good customer service?
    • Is service better in small shops or large stores?
    • Will machines replace shop assistants?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'm going to talk about the excellent service I received from a small electronics repair shop near my university. A few months ago my laptop suddenly stopped charging, two days before an important deadline. I was in a panic, because the official service centre told me the repair would take two weeks. A classmate recommended this little shop, so I took it there the same afternoon. The owner, a young man called Timur, opened the laptop in front of me and found the fault within ten minutes. It was a damaged charging port. What impressed me was what he did next. He explained the problem in simple terms and showed me the part. He told me the price before starting, and it was half of what I'd expected. Then, seeing how worried I was, he stayed after closing time to finish it that evening. He even lent me a spare charger. I thought the service was outstanding because he was honest, fast and treated my problem as if it were his own. I've since sent at least five friends to him.

    Лексика: be in a panic — паниковать; fault — неисправность; in simple terms — простыми словами; spare — запасной; outstanding — выдающийся
    Разбор: Past Perfect (half of what I'd expected), причастный оборот (seeing how worried I was), as if it were his own — сослагательное. Result в Present Perfect (I've since sent).
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. What is good customer service?

      Listening to the customer, being honest about what you can do, and solving the problem quickly. Politeness matters, but I think reliability matters more. A friendly smile is useless if the problem isn't fixed.

    2. Is service better in small shops or large stores?

      In small shops it tends to be more personal, because the owner knows the regular customers and has a reputation to protect. Large stores offer more choice and clearer return policies, but you're often just a number.

    3. Will machines replace shop assistants?

      For simple tasks they already have. Self-service checkouts are everywhere. But I think people will still want human advice when they're buying something complicated or expensive, or when something goes wrong.

    32. Describe a time when you saved some money to buy something special.NEW
    You should say:
    • what you wanted to buy
    • how long you saved
    • how you saved the money
    • and explain how you felt when you bought it
    Part 3:
    • Should children learn to save money?
    • Why do some people find it hard to save?
    • Is it better to save or to spend while you are young?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'd like to talk about the time I saved up for my first proper laptop, which was about three years ago, when I was in my final year of school. At that time I was using an old family computer that froze every ten minutes, and I'd just become interested in video editing, so I desperately needed something faster. The model I had my eye on cost roughly six hundred dollars, which was a fortune for a teenager, and my parents made it clear that if I wanted it, I'd have to earn it myself. So I came up with a plan. I started tutoring two younger kids from my neighbourhood in maths, twice a week, and I also cut back on little things like snacks and taxi rides. I kept the cash in an envelope at the back of my drawer and wrote the running total on it, which was surprisingly motivating. It took me almost eight months, and there were moments when I was tempted to spend the money on a new phone instead. When I finally walked into the shop and paid in cash, I felt incredibly proud. Honestly, the laptop itself wasn't the best part. What mattered was knowing that I'd bought it with money I had earned.

    Лексика: have my eye on — присмотреть; cost a fortune — стоить целое состояние; come up with a plan — придумать план; cut back on — сократить расходы на; be tempted to — испытывать соблазн
    Разбор: Past Continuous для фона (I was using), Past Perfect (I'd just become, I'd bought), эмфаза What mattered was…. Ответ проходит по всем пунктам: что, сколько копил, как, что чувствовал.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. Should children learn to save money?

      Definitely. If children get pocket money and have to save for the things they want, they learn that money is limited. It's a far better lesson than simply being told that things are expensive.

    2. Why do some people find it hard to save?

      For many it's simply that their income barely covers their costs. But there's a psychological side too. Shops and apps make spending effortless, and the pleasure of buying is immediate, whereas the reward of saving is far away.

    3. Is it better to save or to spend while you are young?

      A balance, I'd say. It's sensible to put something aside for emergencies. But youth is also the time to travel and invest in education, so I wouldn't save every penny.

    33. Describe a time when you changed your opinion about something important.
    You should say:
    • what the opinion was
    • why you held it
    • what made you change it
    • and explain how you feel about it now
    Part 3:
    • Why are some people unwilling to change their minds?
    • Does social media make people more or less open-minded?
    • Is it a sign of weakness to change your opinion?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'd like to talk about how I changed my mind about living abroad. Until about two years ago, I was absolutely convinced that I would leave my country after graduating and never come back. I held that opinion because everyone around me seemed to think the same. It was almost taken for granted that success meant a job in Europe or America, and I'd never really questioned it. What changed my mind was a summer exchange programme. I spent two months at a university in Germany. I loved the experience, and I learned a great deal, but I also saw things I hadn't expected. Some of the international students I met were quite lonely, working long hours far from their families. At the same time, I started noticing how much was changing at home, with new companies opening and real opportunities for people with international experience. So my view is now more balanced. I still want to do a master's degree abroad, but I see it as a way of gaining skills to bring back. I feel much calmer about the future than I did.

    Лексика: be convinced that — быть убеждённым; take for granted — считать само собой разумеющимся; question — подвергать сомнению; balanced view — взвешенный взгляд; gain skills — приобретать навыки
    Разбор: Чёткая схема «прежнее мнение → причина → что изменило → нынешнее мнение». Past Perfect (I'd never questioned, hadn't expected), сравнение than I did.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. Why are some people unwilling to change their minds?

      Often because their opinions are tied to their identity or their group. Admitting you were wrong can feel like losing face. People also tend to look only for information that supports what they already believe.

    2. Does social media make people more or less open-minded?

      I think it does both. In theory it exposes us to every point of view. In practice, the systems show us more of what we already like, so many people end up hearing only opinions similar to their own.

    3. Is it a sign of weakness to change your opinion?

      Quite the opposite. It takes confidence to say, 'I was wrong.' Someone who never changes their mind, whatever the evidence, isn't strong, just stubborn. Of course, changing it every week would be a different problem.

    34. Describe a time when you had to change a plan you had made.
    You should say:
    • what the plan was
    • why you had to change it
    • what you did instead
    • and explain how you felt about the change
    Part 3:
    • Is it better to plan everything or to be spontaneous?
    • How do people usually react to unexpected changes?
    • Are young people good at planning?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'd like to describe a time last summer when a trip I'd planned for months fell through at the last minute. Three friends and I had arranged to spend a week hiking in the mountains. We'd booked a guesthouse, bought train tickets and even drawn up a route for each day. Then, two days before we were due to leave, there were heavy rains in the region, and the authorities closed the road to the valley because of the risk of landslides. So we had no choice but to change everything. After a rather gloomy evening of phone calls, one of my friends suggested going in the opposite direction, to a desert area with an old fortress and a lake that none of us had ever seen. We managed to get a partial refund, found a driver, and left a day later than planned. As for how I felt, I was bitterly disappointed at first. I'd been looking forward to those mountains for so long. But the new trip turned out to be wonderful. We swam in the lake at sunset and slept in a traditional tent. It taught me that a spoiled plan isn't necessarily a spoiled holiday.

    Лексика: fall through — сорваться; be due to leave — должны были уехать; landslide — оползень; refund — возврат денег; turn out to be — оказаться
    Разбор: Past Perfect (I'd planned, we'd booked) и Past Perfect Continuous (I'd been looking forward to). Конструкция had no choice but to…. Фразовые глаголы fall through, turn out.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. Is it better to plan everything or to be spontaneous?

      It depends on the situation. For exams or a big journey, careful planning saves a lot of trouble. But if every minute of your free time is scheduled, there's no room for pleasant surprises. I try to plan the essentials and leave the rest open.

    2. How do people usually react to unexpected changes?

      Most people are annoyed at first, especially if they've invested time or money. How they cope afterwards varies. Flexible people look for an alternative quite quickly, whereas others stay upset for days.

    3. Are young people good at planning?

      Not always. Many live from day to day and leave things until the last minute. On the other hand, they're usually good at adapting when something goes wrong, which is a useful skill in itself.

    35. Describe a time when you had to get up very early.
    You should say:
    • when it was
    • why you had to get up early
    • what you did
    • and explain how you felt that day
    Part 3:
    • Are there benefits to getting up early?
    • Why do teenagers find it hard to wake up early?
    • Should schools start later in the morning?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'd like to talk about the morning I had to get up at half past three to catch a flight. It was in January last year, and I was flying to Istanbul for a student conference, which was my first trip abroad on my own. The flight left at six, and I'd been told to be at the airport three hours before. I'm not a morning person at all, so I was nervous about oversleeping. I set three alarms and asked my father to knock on my door as well. In the end I hardly slept. I kept waking up to check the clock. When the alarm finally went off, it was pitch dark and freezing. I had a quick shower, drank some tea, and my father drove me through completely empty streets, which was strangely beautiful. Check-in went smoothly, and I watched the sunrise from the plane. As for how I felt that day, I was running on adrenaline until lunchtime, and then exhaustion hit me in the middle of the opening session. I remember struggling to keep my eyes open. Still, it was worth every lost hour of sleep.

    Лексика: oversleep — проспать; go off — зазвенеть (о будильнике); pitch dark — кромешная тьма; run on adrenaline — держаться на адреналине; be worth — стоить того
    Разбор: Past Perfect (I'd been told), keep + -ing (kept waking up), remember + -ing (remember struggling). As for how I felt… — переход к последнему пункту.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. Are there benefits to getting up early?

      Yes, quite a few. The early hours are quiet, so you can get a lot done without interruptions. People who rise early often say they feel more in control of their day. It only works if you also go to bed early, of course.

    2. Why do teenagers find it hard to wake up early?

      It's largely biological. During adolescence the body clock shifts later, so teenagers don't feel sleepy until late at night. Add phones and homework, and they simply aren't getting enough sleep.

    3. Should schools start later in the morning?

      I think there's a good case for it. Studies suggest that when lessons begin later, attendance and concentration improve. The difficulty is practical. It would clash with parents' working hours and after-school activities.

    36. Describe a time when you watched a live sports event.
    You should say:
    • what the event was
    • where you watched it
    • who you were with
    • and explain how you felt about it
    Part 3:
    • Why do people enjoy watching sport live?
    • Is it better to play sport or to watch it?
    • Do sports stars have too much influence on young people?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'm going to describe a football match I watched at the national stadium about a year ago. It was a World Cup qualifier between our national team and a strong opponent, and tickets had sold out within hours. I went with my father and my younger brother, and it was the first time any of us had been to such an important game. We got there two hours early, and the atmosphere outside was already incredible, with drums, flags and thousands of people in blue shirts. The match itself was tense. Our team went a goal down in the first half, and the whole stadium fell silent. Then, about ten minutes from the end, we equalised, and in the last minute of added time we scored again. I've never heard a noise like it. Thirty thousand people were jumping, and complete strangers were hugging each other. As for my feelings, I went through everything in ninety minutes: frustration, hope and pure joy. I lost my voice for two days. Watching on television is more comfortable, but it can't compare with being part of that crowd.

    Лексика: sell out — быть распроданным; go a goal down — пропустить гол; equalise — сравнять счёт; added time — добавленное время; can't compare with — не идёт в сравнение с
    Разбор: Past Perfect (had sold out, had been), Past Continuous для кульминации (were jumping, were hugging), Present Perfect + превосходное (I've never heard a noise like it). Двоеточие-перечисление эмоций.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. Why do people enjoy watching sport live?

      Because of the atmosphere. You feel the tension together with thousands of other people, and that shared emotion is impossible to reproduce at home. There's also the thrill of knowing that anything can happen.

    2. Is it better to play sport or to watch it?

      Playing is obviously better for your health, and you learn teamwork. But watching has its value too. It gives people something to share and talk about. Ideally, I'd say do both.

    3. Do sports stars have too much influence on young people?

      They certainly have a lot. Children copy their hairstyles and their behaviour, good and bad. I don't think that's a problem when athletes set a good example, but when they behave badly, it matters more than they realise.

    37. Describe a time when you worked with other people in a group.
    You should say:
    • what the task was
    • who you worked with
    • what your role was
    • and explain how well the group worked together
    Part 3:
    • What makes a good team member?
    • Is group work more effective than working alone?
    • What should a team leader do when members disagree?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'd like to talk about a group project I did in my second year at university. The task was to design a marketing plan for a local business and present it to the class at the end of the term. There were five of us, chosen by the lecturer, so we didn't know each other well. My role was coordinator. I wasn't the leader exactly, but I kept track of the deadlines, booked rooms for our meetings and put the final slides together. At the beginning, things didn't go smoothly. Two members had very strong opinions and argued about almost everything, while another hardly spoke. We lost the first two weeks without deciding anything. What helped was dividing the work clearly according to people's strengths. The one who loved numbers did the budget, the quiet one turned out to be an excellent designer, and the two talkers handled the presentation. After that we worked surprisingly well together. We got one of the highest marks in the class. I learned that a group doesn't need everyone to be the same. It needs everyone to know what they're responsible for.

    Лексика: keep track of — следить за; go smoothly — идти гладко; strengths — сильные стороны; turn out to be — оказаться; be responsible for — отвечать за
    Разбор: Контраст at the beginning… / what helped was… / after that…. Эмфаза What helped was dividing…. Параллельная структура в описании ролей.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. What makes a good team member?

      Someone who is reliable, does what they promised on time and communicates openly. Being willing to listen and to compromise matters as much as talent. One brilliant person who ignores everyone else can ruin a team.

    2. Is group work more effective than working alone?

      It depends on the task. For complex problems that need different skills, a group usually produces better results. For work that requires deep concentration, such as writing, people are often faster alone.

    3. What should a team leader do when members disagree?

      Listen to both sides before deciding anything, and bring the discussion back to the common goal. If people still can't agree, the leader has to make a decision and explain the reasons clearly.

    38. Describe a time when you wrote a message or email and had to wait a long time for a reply.
    You should say:
    • who you wrote to
    • what the message was about
    • how long you waited
    • and explain how you felt while waiting
    Part 3:
    • Why do people expect instant replies today?
    • Is email becoming old-fashioned?
    • Is it better to discuss important matters face to face?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'd like to talk about an email I sent to a professor at a university abroad when I was applying for a summer research programme. It was about a year and a half ago. The application required a letter from a member of staff who was willing to supervise me, so I wrote to a professor whose articles I'd read. I spent two days on that message, explaining my background, why her research interested me and what I hoped to learn. Then I waited. A week passed, then two. I checked my inbox dozens of times a day, including the spam folder. By the third week I was convinced she'd deleted it without reading it. As for how I felt, it was a mixture of anxiety and embarrassment. I kept rereading my message, looking for mistakes that might have put her off. I was about to give up when, after almost five weeks, a reply arrived. She apologised, explained that she'd been doing fieldwork with no internet, and agreed to supervise me. I learned two things: that silence doesn't always mean no, and that I should send a polite reminder much sooner.

    Лексика: supervise — руководить (научной работой); inbox — входящие; put someone off — оттолкнуть; be about to — собираться вот-вот; fieldwork — полевая работа
    Разбор: Past Perfect (I'd read, she'd deleted, she'd been doing), модальность в прошлом (might have put her off), was about to… when…. Двоеточие с двумя выводами.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. Why do people expect instant replies today?

      Because technology has made it possible. With messaging apps we can see when someone is online and whether they've read our message, so a delay of a few hours feels like being ignored.

    2. Is email becoming old-fashioned?

      Among friends, yes. Most people use messaging apps. But in professional life it's still essential, especially for anything formal or anything that needs a written record.

    3. Is it better to discuss important matters face to face?

      I think so. Tone of voice and facial expressions prevent a lot of misunderstanding. Written messages are easy to misread. For bad news or a sensitive topic, meeting in person, or at least a call, is far better.

    39. Describe a time you made an important decision and were pleased with the result.
    You should say:
    • what the decision was
    • when you made it
    • who helped you decide
    • and explain why you were pleased
    Part 3:
    • Should young people make important decisions alone?
    • Do people make better decisions quickly or slowly?
    • What decisions are hardest for young adults?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'd like to talk about my decision to change my university course at the end of my first year. I'd originally enrolled to study law, largely because my parents thought it was a secure profession. But by the second term I realised I was forcing myself to open the textbooks, while I was spending my free time reading about economics. I made the decision in May, just before the deadline for transfer applications. It wasn't easy, because switching meant taking two extra exams and possibly disappointing my family. Several people helped me. I talked to a lecturer in the economics department, who let me sit in on a few classes. My older cousin, who had changed careers herself, told me that one difficult conversation is better than forty years in the wrong job. And in the end my parents were far more understanding than I'd feared. I'm pleased with the result because everything feels different now. I look forward to lectures, my marks have gone up, and I've already done an internship that I loved. I only wish I'd had the courage to do it sooner.

    Лексика: enrol — поступить, записаться; secure profession — надёжная профессия; switch — сменить; sit in on a class — посетить занятие как слушатель; internship — стажировка
    Разбор: Past Perfect (I'd originally enrolled, had changed, than I'd feared), I only wish I'd had… — сожаление о прошлом. Present Perfect для результата (my marks have gone up).
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. Should young people make important decisions alone?

      They should certainly listen to advice, since older people have experience they lack. But the final choice ought to be theirs, because they're the ones who'll live with it. A decision made for you is hard to commit to.

    2. Do people make better decisions quickly or slowly?

      It depends on the decision. For everyday matters, going with your first instinct is usually fine. For anything with long-term consequences, like a career or a large purchase, it's worth sleeping on it.

    3. What decisions are hardest for young adults?

      Choosing what to study and where to live, I'd say, and later whether to accept a job that pays well but doesn't interest them. These choices feel huge because they seem to close other doors.

    40. Describe a problem you had with some technology, for example a computer or a phone.
    You should say:
    • what the technology was
    • what the problem was
    • how you solved it
    • and explain how you felt
    Part 3:
    • Are people too dependent on technology?
    • Why do older people often struggle with new devices?
    • Should companies make products easier to repair?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'd like to describe a problem I had with my phone during a trip last year. I was travelling alone to another city for a friend's wedding, and I'd saved everything on my phone: the train ticket, the address and the map. About an hour into the journey, the screen simply went black. It wasn't the battery. I'd charged it that morning. I tried holding the buttons down, but nothing happened. I'm embarrassed to say I panicked a little, because I suddenly realised I didn't know a single phone number by heart, not even my friend's. In the end, the solution was quite old-fashioned. The woman sitting opposite me lent me her phone, and I logged into my email, where I found the ticket and the address, and wrote them down on paper. At the station I asked a taxi driver for directions. A repair shop later told me it was a software fault, and they fixed it in twenty minutes. The experience made me feel rather foolish. I now keep a paper copy of important details and I've memorised three phone numbers.

    Лексика: go black — погаснуть; know by heart — знать наизусть; log into — войти в (аккаунт); old-fashioned — старомодный; software fault — программный сбой
    Разбор: Past Perfect (I'd saved, I'd charged), Past Continuous для фона, результат в настоящем (I now keep… I've memorised). I'm embarrassed to say… — естественная вставка.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. Are people too dependent on technology?

      I think many of us are. We rely on our phones for directions, payments and even remembering birthdays. That's fine when everything works, but it leaves us helpless the moment something breaks.

    2. Why do older people often struggle with new devices?

      Mainly because they didn't grow up with them, so the logic of menus and icons isn't intuitive. Devices also change very fast. They may be afraid of pressing the wrong button and breaking something.

    3. Should companies make products easier to repair?

      Yes, I think they should. At the moment it's often cheaper to replace a device than to fix it, which creates a huge amount of waste. Replaceable batteries and available spare parts would save money and resources.

    Things, media and ideas

    41. Describe an exciting book that you enjoyed reading.NEW
    You should say:
    • what the book was
    • what it was about
    • when you read it
    • and explain why you found it exciting
    Part 3:
    • Do people read less than in the past?
    • Are e-books better than paper books?
    • How can parents encourage children to read?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'd like to talk about The Martian by Andy Weir, which is one of the most exciting books I've ever read. I read it about two years ago, during the summer holidays, after a friend insisted that I borrow his copy. It's a science-fiction novel about an astronaut who is accidentally left behind on Mars when his crew believes he's dead. He has to survive alone for more than a year, with limited food and no way of contacting Earth. I found it exciting for several reasons. Every time he solves one problem, such as growing potatoes inside his shelter, something else goes wrong, so the tension never drops. What I liked even more was his attitude. Instead of despairing, he treats each disaster as a puzzle, and he keeps a diary full of dark humour. The science is explained so clearly that I actually understood it. I finished the last hundred pages at three in the morning because I simply couldn't put it down. It left me with the feeling that almost any problem can be solved if you break it into small enough pieces.

    Лексика: be left behind — быть оставленным; tension — напряжение; despair — отчаиваться; dark humour — чёрный юмор; couldn't put it down — не мог оторваться
    Разбор: Present Simple для пересказа сюжета, so… that, эмфаза What I liked even more was…. Idiom couldn't put it down. Можно заменить на свою книгу, сохранив схему.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. Do people read less than in the past?

      I think they read fewer books but more text overall: messages, articles, posts. What has declined is long, concentrated reading. Many people say they simply can't focus on a novel the way they used to.

    2. Are e-books better than paper books?

      They're more practical. You can carry a hundred in your pocket and they're cheaper. But many readers, including me, remember a story better on paper, and a printed book doesn't tempt you to check your messages.

    3. How can parents encourage children to read?

      Mostly by example. If children see their parents reading for pleasure, it seems a normal thing to do. Reading aloud at bedtime and letting children choose their own books help as well. Forcing them usually backfires.

    42. Describe an interview with a famous person that you saw, heard or read.NEW
    You should say:
    • who the person was
    • where you saw or read the interview
    • what they talked about
    • and explain what you thought of it
    Part 3:
    • Why are people interested in the lives of celebrities?
    • Do famous people have a right to privacy?
    • Are journalists always honest in interviews?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'd like to describe an interview with the tennis player Novak Djokovic that I watched online a few months ago. It was a long conversation on a well-known news programme, lasting about half an hour. The interviewer asked him about his childhood, his rivalry with other great players and how he deals with pressure. A few things stayed with me. He talked about growing up during the war in his country and practising in an empty swimming pool because there was nowhere else. He said those years taught him to appreciate every opportunity. He also spoke very openly about nerves. I'd always assumed that champions don't feel fear, but he said that he feels it in every big match and that the difference lies in what you do with it. He described specific breathing techniques he uses between points. I thought it was a remarkably honest interview. He didn't give the usual polished answers, and he admitted mistakes he'd made earlier in his career. It changed my view of him. I'd seen him as a rather cold figure, but he came across as thoughtful and surprisingly humble.

    Лексика: rivalry — соперничество; deal with pressure — справляться с давлением; assume — предполагать; come across as — производить впечатление; humble — скромный
    Разбор: Косвенная речь (He said those years taught him…, he said that he feels…), Past Perfect (I'd always assumed, he'd made, I'd seen him as). Вывод о смене мнения. Подставь своё интервью и проверь факты.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. Why are people interested in the lives of celebrities?

      Partly curiosity. Their lives look glamorous and very different from ours. But I think people also look for something to identify with. When a star talks about failure or family problems, it makes them seem human.

    2. Do famous people have a right to privacy?

      Yes, they do. Being well known is part of their job, but that doesn't make their children or their medical records public property. I think there's a clear line between their work and their private life.

    3. Are journalists always honest in interviews?

      Most try to be, but not all. Interviews can be edited so that a remark sounds different out of context, and some journalists ask questions designed to provoke. That's why it's worth watching the whole interview.

    43. Describe an activity you do regularly that you think is a waste of time.NEW
    You should say:
    • what the activity is
    • how often you do it
    • why you do it
    • and explain why you think it wastes your time
    Part 3:
    • How do people waste time nowadays?
    • Is it important to manage time well?
    • Do smartphones save time or waste it?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'd like to talk about something I do almost every day and consider a complete waste of time: scrolling through short videos on my phone. I'd estimate that I spend at least an hour a day on it, usually in small pieces: ten minutes after waking up, a bit on the bus, and then the worst session, in bed before going to sleep. As for why I do it, the honest answer is habit. It requires no effort at all. When I'm tired or bored, my thumb opens the app before I've even made a decision. The videos are designed to keep you watching, and each one is so short that you always think, just one more. I think it's a waste of time because I get absolutely nothing from it. If you asked me to name three videos I watched yesterday, I couldn't. It also leaves me feeling more tired, not more relaxed, and it eats into time I could spend reading or sleeping. I've recently moved the app off my home screen and set a thirty-minute limit, which has helped a little, though I haven't beaten the habit yet.

    Лексика: scroll through — листать; estimate — оценивать; require no effort — не требовать усилий; eat into time — съедать время; beat a habit — побороть привычку
    Разбор: Условное II (If you asked me…, I couldn't), so short that…, Present Perfect для недавних действий (I've recently moved… I haven't beaten). Честный, самокритичный тон звучит естественно.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. How do people waste time nowadays?

      Mostly on their phones: social media, short videos and games. Unnecessary meetings at work are another big one. And a lot of time is lost simply switching between tasks instead of finishing one.

    2. Is it important to manage time well?

      Extremely. Time is the one resource you can't get back. People who plan their day and decide what matters most achieve more and are usually less stressed.

    3. Do smartphones save time or waste it?

      Both. They save time when we use them as tools, for navigation, banking or quick messages. They waste it when we pick them up with no purpose. The device isn't the problem. It's how we use it.

    44. Describe a law to help the environment which you think your country should have.
    You should say:
    • what the law would be
    • who it would affect
    • how it would work
    • and explain why your country needs it
    Part 3:
    • Are laws or education more effective in protecting the environment?
    • Should individuals or companies take more responsibility?
    • Why do some people ignore environmental rules?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'd like to talk about a law that I think my country should introduce: a deposit on plastic bottles and drinks cans. The idea is simple. When you buy a drink, you pay a small extra amount, say five per cent of the price, and you get it back when you return the empty container to a shop or a collection machine. It would affect almost everyone: consumers, who would have to bring bottles back; shops, which would need space for the machines; and drinks companies, which would be responsible for recycling what is collected. As for how it would work, the system already exists in countries like Germany, where more than ninety per cent of bottles are returned. I believe we need it for several reasons. At the moment, plastic bottles are everywhere, in rivers, in parks and beside the roads, and very little is recycled. Fines for littering don't work because nobody is ever caught. A deposit gives people a direct financial reason to do the right thing. It would also create some income for people who collect bottles others have thrown away.

    Лексика: deposit — залог; container — тара; fine — штраф; littering — выбрасывание мусора; financial reason — финансовый стимул
    Разбор: Условное II для гипотетического закона (It would affect…, shops would need…). Перечисление с придаточными who/which. As for how it would work… — переход по пунктам карточки.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. Are laws or education more effective in protecting the environment?

      I think you need both. Education changes attitudes in the long run, especially among children. But it's slow, and some people will always ignore advice. Laws with real penalties produce results much faster.

    2. Should individuals or companies take more responsibility?

      Companies, I'd say, because the scale of their impact is so much greater. One factory can pollute more than a whole town. But individuals aren't innocent. Companies produce what we choose to buy.

    3. Why do some people ignore environmental rules?

      Often because following them costs time or money, and the chance of being punished is small. Some people simply don't believe that one person's actions make a difference.

    45. Describe a story you like that has animals in it (a book, children's story or film).
    You should say:
    • what the story is
    • when you first read or saw it
    • what happens in it
    • and explain why you like it
    Part 3:
    • Why do children's stories often have animal characters?
    • Should children have pets?
    • Is it right to keep animals in zoos?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'd like to talk about The Jungle Book, the story of a boy called Mowgli who is raised by wolves in the Indian jungle. I first came across it as an animated film when I was about six, and I read the original stories by Rudyard Kipling a few years later. In the story, a small child is found in the forest and adopted by a wolf family. He is taught the laws of the jungle by a bear, Baloo, and protected by a black panther, Bagheera. His great enemy is the tiger Shere Khan, who wants to kill him. As Mowgli grows up, he has to decide whether he belongs with the animals or with humans. I like it for several reasons. As a child I simply loved the adventure and the idea of talking to animals. Now I appreciate the characters more. Each animal has a distinct personality: the bear is lazy and warm, the panther is wise and serious. Underneath, it's really a story about growing up and finding where you belong, which is something everyone goes through.

    Лексика: be raised by — быть выращенным; come across — наткнуться, познакомиться; adopt — усыновить; belong with — быть своим среди; go through — проходить через
    Разбор: Present Simple и пассив для пересказа (is found, is taught, protected by). Контраст as a child… / now…. Двоеточие с примерами характеров.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. Why do children's stories often have animal characters?

      Because animals make ideas simple and safe. A greedy fox or a brave mouse teaches a lesson without pointing at any real person. Children also naturally love animals, so the stories hold their attention.

    2. Should children have pets?

      If the family can look after it properly, yes. A pet teaches responsibility and kindness. But it shouldn't be bought on impulse. An animal is a commitment of ten years or more.

    3. Is it right to keep animals in zoos?

      It's a difficult issue. Good zoos protect endangered species and educate the public. But many animals clearly suffer in small enclosures. I'd support zoos only where the animals have enough space and the main aim is conservation.

    46. Describe a type of food that you like to eat on special occasions.
    You should say:
    • what the food is
    • when you eat it
    • how it is prepared
    • and explain why you like it
    Part 3:
    • Why is food so important in celebrations?
    • Are traditional dishes disappearing?
    • Do young people cook less than their parents did?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'd like to talk about plov, the rice dish that is at the centre of almost every celebration in my country. It's eaten at weddings, at the birth of a child, on holidays and whenever important guests arrive. In its basic form it's made of rice, lamb or beef, yellow and orange carrots, and onions, cooked together in a large iron pot called a kazan. Many families add chickpeas, raisins or whole heads of garlic. As for how it's prepared, there's a strict order. First the oil is heated and the meat is browned, then the onions and carrots are added, and finally the rice is laid on top and left to steam without stirring. Traditionally it's cooked over a wood fire, and for big occasions the cook is always a man, often a specialist hired for the day. I like it for its taste, of course. The carrots turn sweet and the rice absorbs all the flavour. But it's more than food. Everyone eats from a shared dish, and the smell alone tells you that something good is happening.

    Лексика: chickpeas — нут; raisins — изюм; brown the meat — обжарить мясо; steam — готовиться на пару; shared dish — общее блюдо
    Разбор: Пассив для процесса (is heated, is browned, are added, is laid), маркеры последовательности First… then… finally…. But it's more than food — переход к эмоциональной причине.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. Why is food so important in celebrations?

      Because sharing a meal is one of the oldest ways of showing hospitality and belonging. Special dishes take time and effort, so preparing them shows guests they're valued. The tastes also connect people with memories.

    2. Are traditional dishes disappearing?

      A few are, especially those that take hours to prepare. People are busier and often prefer something quick. But the dishes linked to holidays seem safe, because nobody wants a celebration without them.

    3. Do young people cook less than their parents did?

      Generally, yes. Ready meals and delivery apps make it easy not to. Many young people also live alone and don't see the point of cooking for one. Interestingly, cooking videos have made some of them curious again.

    47. Describe an advertisement you saw with a famous person in it.
    You should say:
    • what was advertised
    • who the famous person was
    • where you saw it
    • and explain what you thought of it
    Part 3:
    • Why do companies use celebrities in advertising?
    • Should advertising to children be restricted?
    • Do advertisements influence what you buy?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'd like to describe an advertisement for a mobile bank that I saw on television and on billboards around my city last year. It featured a famous footballer from our national team. In the advert he is shown in ordinary situations: paying for bread at a small shop, sending money to his mother, splitting the bill with friends after a match. Each time, he simply taps his phone. At the end he looks at the camera and says the slogan, something like, 'Fast, like a counter-attack.' I thought it was quite effective, for a few reasons. He was well chosen. He has a reputation for being modest and reliable, which is exactly the image a bank wants. The advert also had some humour. In one scene his teammates all pretend to have forgotten their wallets. And it showed the product actually being used instead of just listing features. That said, I don't believe for a moment that he uses that bank himself. I didn't open an account because of him, but I did remember the name, which I suppose was the point.

    Лексика: billboard — рекламный щит; feature — показывать, включать; split the bill — разделить счёт; slogan — слоган; reputation for — репутация (кого-то какого-то)
    Разбор: Present Simple для описания рекламы, пассив (he is shown, being used), эмфаза I did remember the name. That said… вводит критическую оговорку.
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. Why do companies use celebrities in advertising?

      Because a familiar face attracts attention instantly and people transfer their feelings about the star to the product. If you admire an athlete, some of that trust rubs off on whatever he's holding.

    2. Should advertising to children be restricted?

      I think it should. Young children can't tell the difference between information and persuasion. Adverts for sweets, fast food and expensive toys put pressure on them and on their parents.

    3. Do advertisements influence what you buy?

      More than I'd like to admit. I don't rush out and buy things, but when I'm choosing between two similar products, I tend to pick the name I recognise, and I recognise it because of advertising.

    48. Describe an ambition you have had for a very long time.
    You should say:
    • what the ambition is
    • when you first had it
    • what you have done to achieve it
    • and explain why it is important to you
    Part 3:
    • Are ambitious people happier?
    • Do parents put too much pressure on children to succeed?
    • How do ambitions change as people get older?
    Образец ответа (Band 8), разбор и ответы Part 3

    I'd like to talk about an ambition I've had since I was about twelve: to study for a master's degree at a university abroad. It began when a cousin of mine won a scholarship to study in Britain. I remember the whole family gathering to see her off at the airport, and thinking that I wanted that to be me one day. Since then I've been working towards it step by step. I started taking English seriously at school, and I've kept my university marks high, because scholarships are very competitive. Last year I took part in a summer school in Europe to see what studying abroad is really like. At the moment I'm preparing for the IELTS exam, and I've started researching programmes and drafting a personal statement. It's important to me for several reasons. I want to learn from specialists who are leaders in my field, and I want to test myself in an unfamiliar environment. But above all, I'd like to bring that knowledge home. I'd be the second person in my family to do it, and I know how proud my parents would be.

    Лексика: win a scholarship — получить стипендию; see someone off — провожать; competitive — конкурентный; draft — составлять черновик; personal statement — мотивационное письмо
    Разбор: Present Perfect и Present Perfect Continuous для длительности (I've had since…, I've been working towards it), Present Continuous для текущего этапа. Условное в конце (how proud my parents would be).
    Part 3 — образцы ответов
    1. Are ambitious people happier?

      Not necessarily. Ambition gives people direction and satisfaction when they achieve something. But very ambitious people are often never content. As soon as they reach one goal, they want the next.

    2. Do parents put too much pressure on children to succeed?

      In many families, yes. Parents want the best, but when the pressure is constant, children become anxious and afraid of failure. Encouragement works better than comparison with other people's children.

    3. How do ambitions change as people get older?
